title: Pork Chile Verde (Muy Delish)
lines: Recipe credit: Ana Frias of Muy Delish. Original: Pork Chile Verde.
Yield: 6 servings | Prep: 20 minutes | Cook: 1 hour 20 minutes
Ingredients
2 pounds lean pork, cubed
2 garlic cloves for pork
1/4 onion for pork
1 bay leaf
1 teaspoon salt
1/2 teaspoon black pepper
9 large tomatillos, husked and rinsed
1 jalapeno, stemmed and seeded
1 serrano, stemmed and seeded
2 garlic cloves for salsa
1/4 onion for salsa
1/2 cup packed cilantro
1 teaspoon chicken bouillon
1/2 teaspoon sugar
1 1/2 cups reserved pork cooking liquid
Water to cover pork; extra salt to taste
Directions
Cover pork with water; add its garlic, onion, bay, salt, and pepper. Bring to a boil; skim foam. Simmer about 1 hour.
Reserve the listed cooking liquid; discard bay. Let remaining liquid evaporate and lightly brown pork.
Dry-roast tomatillos, peppers, salsa garlic, and salsa onion in a skillet until softened and blistered. Cool.
Blend roasted vegetables, cilantro, bouillon, sugar, and two-thirds of reserved liquid.
Add salsa to pork. Rinse blender with remaining reserved liquid; add to pot. Cover; simmer gently 20 minutes. Season and serve.
Notes
Rice, beans, and tortillas are optional sides. For fractional vegetables, measure by weight; omit bay fragments when serving. Time depends on pork tenderness, not portion count.

title: Thai Yellow Curry with Shrimp
lines: Yield: 4 servings | Prep: 5 minutes | Cook: 25 minutes
Ingredients
1 1/2 pounds raw shrimp, peeled and deveined
2 tablespoons fish sauce for shrimp
2 cups coconut milk
5 tablespoons Thai yellow curry paste
2 cups diced tomatoes
1 tablespoon fish sauce for curry
1 tablespoon palm or brown sugar
Salt and pepper, to taste
Cilantro or Thai basil, lime, chili flakes, and cooked jasmine rice, for serving
Directions
Toss shrimp with its fish sauce and a little pepper; refrigerate 10 minutes while starting the sauce. Salt only if needed.
Heat coconut milk in a skillet over medium heat for about 10 minutes. Continue even if the oil does not separate.
Stir in yellow curry paste. Cook gently for 3-4 minutes, stirring.
Add tomatoes, remaining fish sauce, and sugar. Simmer 5 minutes.
Add shrimp and marinade; cook 2-3 minutes, or until shrimp are opaque throughout. Adjust seasoning; serve with rice, lime, and herbs.
Notes
Paste brands vary in heat and salt; start with less if desired. Rice is separate from curry quantities. Scaled spoon measures are rounded; keep shrimp cooking time brief and judge doneness.

title: Thai Green Curry Chicken
lines: Yield: 8 servings | Prep: 30 minutes | Cook: 20 minutes
Ingredients
1 1/2 pounds thinly sliced boneless chicken
1 tablespoon cornstarch
1 tablespoon water
2 teaspoons oyster sauce
3 tablespoons neutral oil, divided
1 onion, sliced
4 ounces green curry paste; halve for milder curry
5 cups mixed vegetables, cut small
13 1/2 ounces coconut milk
1 1/4 cups chicken stock
1 tablespoon sugar
1 tablespoon fish sauce
1/2 cup basil leaves
Jasmine rice, cooked separately
Directions
Coat chicken with cornstarch, water, oyster sauce, and one-third of the oil.
Heat remaining oil in a skillet over medium-high heat. Brown chicken; transfer to a plate.
Soften onion in the skillet, loosening browned bits with water if needed. Stir in curry paste; cook 5 minutes.
Add vegetables; stir 2 minutes. Add coconut milk, stock, and chicken. Cover; simmer gently about 8 minutes, until vegetables are tender and chicken reaches 165 F.
Stir in sugar, fish sauce, and basil. Serve with jasmine rice.
Notes
Choose green beans, peppers, bamboo shoots, carrots, mushrooms, zucchini, broccoli, or eggplant. Add dense vegetables earlier if needed.
Original yield is 8. Smaller versions are proportional adaptations, with spoon measurements rounded. Use a smaller pan for small batches and judge doneness rather than shortening time automatically.

title: Thai Red Curry with Chicken
lines: Yield: 4 servings | Prep: 10 minutes | Cook: 20 minutes
Ingredients
1 pound thinly sliced chicken thighs
2 tablespoons oil
1 tablespoon ginger paste
1 tablespoon minced garlic
4 tablespoons red curry paste
1 1/2 teaspoons fish sauce
13 ounces coconut milk
1 tablespoon lime juice
1 tablespoon brown sugar
1/2 teaspoon chili flakes, optional
1 red bell pepper, sliced
1 cup chopped green beans
2 tablespoons chopped Thai basil
1 tablespoon cilantro
1 tablespoon cornstarch
2 tablespoons water
Salt to taste
Directions
Fry ginger, garlic, and curry paste in oil over medium heat, 2-3 minutes.
Stir in fish sauce, coconut milk, lime, sugar, and chili flakes; bring to a simmer.
Add chicken; simmer about 8 minutes. Add pepper and beans; cook 4-5 minutes.
Combine cornstarch with water. Stir into curry with herbs; simmer until thickened. Check chicken reaches 165 F. Serve with rice.
Notes
Curry paste heat and salt vary by brand; begin with less for a milder dish. Rice is separate from the curry quantities.
The source yields 4-5 servings; portion calculations here use 4. Measure fractional peppers by weight. Cooking time depends on chicken thickness, not serving count.

title: Chicken Biryani
lines: Yield: 4 servings | Prep: 15 minutes; marinate 30 minutes | Cook: about 30 minutes; rest 10 minutes
Ingredients
500 g chicken
1/2 cup yogurt
1 tablespoon grated ginger
1-2 teaspoons minced garlic
3-4 chopped green chilies
1/2 teaspoon turmeric
1 teaspoon red chili powder
1 teaspoon salt for chicken; 1 teaspoon for rice water
1-2 tablespoons each chopped mint and cilantro for marinade
1 cup basmati rice
2 tablespoons ghee or oil
1 teaspoon cumin seeds
2 tablespoons cashews
1/2-inch cinnamon
2 cloves
2-3 cardamom seeds
1 bay leaf
1 large sliced onion
1 chopped tomato, optional
1 tablespoon ghee for topping
2 tablespoons each mint and cilantro for layering
2 tablespoons milk and 5 saffron threads, optional
Directions
Refrigerate chicken with yogurt, ginger, garlic, chilies, ground spices, salt, and marinade herbs for 30 minutes.
Soak rice 30 minutes; boil in salted water until roughly 80% cooked, then drain.
Heat oil with whole spices and cashews. Soften onion; add tomato, chicken, marinade, and half the layering herbs. Cook 5 minutes.
Layer rice over chicken. Add saffron milk, a splash of water, remaining herbs, and topping ghee. Cover; cook gently 18-20 minutes. Rest 10 minutes; fluff.
Notes
Use a heavy pot. Remove whole spices before serving.
Chicken must reach 165 F at its thickest part. Check before the resting step; continue gentle cooking if needed.

title: One-Day Balanced Menu
lines: Yield: 1 full day | Serving size: each meal or snack as listed
Breakfast
1/2 cup cooked steel-cut oats
1 tablespoon chia seeds, 1/4 cup fresh blueberries, and cinnamon
1 hard-boiled egg
Black coffee or unsweetened green tea
Morning Snack
1 ounce raw almonds or walnuts
1 small cucumber, sliced
Lunch
2 cups mixed leafy greens
4 ounces grilled chicken breast
1/2 cup cherry tomatoes and sliced bell pepper, plus 1/2 avocado
1 tablespoon extra-virgin olive oil with lemon juice
Afternoon Snack
3/4 cup plain unsweetened Greek yogurt
1 tablespoon pumpkin seeds
Dinner
4 ounces baked salmon
1/4 cup cooked quinoa or brown rice
1 1/2 cups roasted broccoli and cauliflower, lightly tossed with olive oil
Optional Evening Snack
1 string cheese or 1/2 cup cottage cheese, if desired
Planning Note
Snacks are optional; include them when they fit your appetite and schedule.
Treat the listed portions as a starting point and adjust them to suit your needs.

title: Three Balanced Favorite-Foods Breakfasts
lines: Yield: 3 breakfast choices | Serving size: 1 complete option
Option 1: Breakfast Scramble
2 eggs scrambled in 1 teaspoon olive oil
1 to 2 tablespoons shredded cheese
1 to 2 lean turkey or chicken sausage links, according to the package serving
1/2 cup skin-on air-fried hash browns
Add bell pepper, spinach, mushrooms, tomatoes, or onions whenever possible
Option 2: Hearty Breakfast Skillet
1/2 cup skin-on air-fried potato cubes
1 sliced lean sausage link
1 cup chopped vegetables, such as bell peppers, spinach, mushrooms, tomatoes, or onions
1 or 2 eggs
1 tablespoon shredded cheese
Option 3: High-Fiber Breakfast Burrito
1 high-fiber tortilla
2 scrambled eggs
1 lean sausage link, crumbled
1/4 cup skin-on roasted potatoes plus 1/2 cup chopped vegetables
1 tablespoon cheese plus salsa or pico de gallo
Breakfast Notes
Serve the potatoes with eggs or sausage and vegetables for a complete breakfast.
Choose coffee or tea and add your preferred creamer, if desired.

title: Crispy Skin-On Air-Fryer Hash Browns
lines: Yield: 2 servings | Serving size: 1/2 cup
Yield: 2 servings | Prep: 10 minutes, plus optional soaking | Cook: 15 to 18 minutes
Ingredients
1 medium russet potato, scrubbed and left unpeeled
1 teaspoon olive oil
1/4 teaspoon garlic powder
1/4 teaspoon smoked or sweet paprika
Black pepper, to taste
Small pinch of salt, optional
Directions
Cut the potato into uniform 1/2-inch cubes.
For extra crispness, soak the cubes in cold water for 15 to 30 minutes. Drain and dry them completely.
Toss with the olive oil, garlic powder, paprika, pepper, and optional salt.
Preheat the air fryer to 400 degrees F. Spread the potatoes in a single layer.
Air-fry for 15 to 18 minutes, shaking every 5 minutes, until browned and tender.
Divide into two equal 1/2-cup portions and serve hot.
Shredded Variation
Grate the scrubbed, unpeeled potato on the large holes of a box grater and squeeze it very dry in a clean towel.
Toss with the same oil and seasonings. Press into a thin layer in a greased basket and air-fry at 380 degrees F for 13 to 15 minutes; flip carefully and cook 4 to 5 minutes more.
Divide into two equal portions.

title: Three-Minute Spinach and Feta Egg Mug
lines: Yield: 1 serving | Serving size: 1 mug
Yield: 1 serving | Prep: 1 minute | Cook: about 2 minutes
Ingredients
2 large eggs
1 tablespoon milk or water
1 loosely packed cup fresh spinach, roughly chopped
1 tablespoon crumbled feta cheese
Black pepper, to taste
Nonstick cooking spray, optional
Directions
Lightly coat a large 16-ounce microwave-safe mug or bowl with cooking spray.
Whisk the eggs with the milk or water. Stir in the spinach, feta, and black pepper.
Microwave on high for 45 seconds and stir. Continue in 15- to 30-second intervals until the eggs are fully set and the center reaches 160 degrees F. Microwave power varies, so watch closely.
Let stand for 1 minute before eating.
Balanced Breakfast Note
Eggs and feta make the mug satisfying, while spinach adds color and freshness. Use less feta if you prefer a milder flavor.

title: Savory Whole-Wheat Bread
lines: Yield: 1 loaf, 16 thin slices | Serving size: 1 slice
Ingredients
2 cups whole-wheat flour
1 1/2 cups bread flour or all-purpose flour
2 1/4 teaspoons instant yeast
1 1/2 teaspoons salt
1 1/4 cups warm water
2 tablespoons olive oil
Optional: rosemary or Italian seasoning, garlic powder, cracked black pepper, or grated Parmesan
Directions
Combine the whole-wheat flour, bread flour, yeast, salt, and any optional seasonings in a large bowl.
Add the warm water and olive oil. Stir until a shaggy dough forms.
Knead for about 8 minutes, until the dough is smooth and elastic.
Place the dough in a lightly oiled bowl, cover, and let rise for 1 to 1 1/2 hours, or until doubled.
Shape the dough and place it in a greased 9-by-5-inch loaf pan.
Cover and let rise again for 45 to 60 minutes.
Bake at 375 degrees F for 30 to 35 minutes, until deeply golden and the loaf sounds hollow when tapped.
Remove from the pan and cool before slicing.

title: Garlic Parmesan Quick Loaf
lines: Yield: 1 loaf, 12 thin slices | Serving size: 1 slice
Ingredients
1/2 cup unsalted butter (1 stick)
2 teaspoons minced garlic (about 2 cloves)
2 cups all-purpose flour
2 teaspoons baking powder
1/2 teaspoon salt
1/2 teaspoon black pepper
1/4 teaspoon baking soda
1 cup shredded Parmesan cheese
1 cup buttermilk
2 large eggs
Directions
Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F and grease a 9-by-5-inch loaf pan.
Melt the butter with the minced garlic, then let it cool briefly.
Whisk together the flour, baking powder, salt, black pepper, baking soda, and Parmesan.
Stir in the buttermilk and garlic butter just until combined.
Mix in the eggs last. Do not overmix.
Spread the batter evenly in the prepared pan.
Bake for 40 to 45 minutes, until golden and a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean.
Cool in the pan for about 10 minutes, then remove and cool slightly before slicing.

title: Easy No-Yeast Pizza Dough
lines: Yield: 2 thin 8-inch crusts, 4 servings | Serving size: 1/2 crust before toppings
Ingredients
2 3/4 cups plus 2 tablespoons all-purpose flour
2 3/4 teaspoons baking powder
1 teaspoon salt
1 tablespoon olive oil
2/3 to 3/4 cup warm water
Optional: 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder
Optional: 1/2 teaspoon Italian seasoning
Directions
Preheat the oven to 425 degrees F. Place a baking sheet or pizza pan in the oven to heat.
Mix the flour, baking powder, salt, and optional seasonings in a large bowl.
Add the olive oil and 2/3 cup warm water.
Stir until a ball forms. If the dough is dry, add the remaining water 1 tablespoon at a time. The dough should be soft but not sticky.
Knead for 3 to 4 minutes.
Divide into two balls and roll each one thin.
Place the dough on the hot baking sheet. For a crisper crust, par-bake for 4 to 5 minutes.
Add sauce, cheese, and desired toppings.
Bake for 10 to 15 minutes, until the crust is browned and the cheese is bubbling.

title: Copycat Pizza Hut Pan Pizza
lines: Yield: 1 eight-inch pizza, 4 slices | Serving size: 1 slice
Ingredients
7 tablespoons plus 1/4 teaspoon warm water, about 105 degrees F
1 tablespoon plus 1 teaspoon nonfat dry milk
1 teaspoon sugar
3/4 teaspoon active dry yeast
1 1/3 cups all-purpose flour
Scant 1/4 teaspoon salt
2 teaspoons olive oil, for the dough
2 tablespoons vegetable or olive oil, for the pan
1/3 cup pizza sauce
4 ounces shredded mozzarella cheese, about 1 cup
Favorite toppings, such as pepperoni, Canadian bacon, sausage, bacon, pineapple, black olives, mushrooms, peppers, onions, or tomatoes
1 tablespoon plus 1 teaspoon butter, melted
1 teaspoon minced garlic, or 1/3 teaspoon garlic powder
Directions
Combine the warm water, dry milk, sugar, and yeast. Stir and let stand for 5 to 10 minutes, until foamy.
Add the 2 teaspoons olive oil, flour, and salt. Stir until combined, then knead by hand or with a stand mixer for about 10 minutes, until soft and smooth.
Coat one 8-inch round cake pan with 2 tablespoons oil, spreading it evenly across the bottom and slightly up the sides.
Roll or press the dough into an 8-inch round and place it in the pan, pressing it to the edges. Cover and let rise in a warm place for 1 to 1 1/2 hours, until puffy and nearly doubled.
Combine the melted butter and garlic. Let it rest for at least 20 minutes so the flavor infuses.
Near the end of the rise, heat the oven to 450 degrees F.
Spread the sauce over the risen dough, leaving about 1 inch uncovered around the edge. Add 3 ounces of mozzarella, your toppings, then the remaining 1 ounce mozzarella.
Bake for 12 to 15 minutes, until the cheese is bubbling and the outer crust is golden brown.
Brush the hot crust edge with garlic butter before serving.
Notes
No dry milk? Use 7 tablespoons plus 1/4 teaspoon warm milk in place of both the water and dry milk.
The 2 tablespoons of oil in the pan are intentional; they create the crisp, rich pan-pizza crust.
Adapted from a recipe by Leigh Anne Wilkes.

title: Emergency Garlic Flatbread
lines: Yield: 6 flatbreads | Serving size: 1 flatbread
Ingredients
2 cups all-purpose flour
2 teaspoons baking powder
1 teaspoon salt
1 teaspoon garlic powder
3/4 cup warm water, plus more if needed
2 tablespoons olive oil
2 tablespoons melted butter
Optional: dried parsley, Italian seasoning, or grated Parmesan
Directions
Whisk the flour, baking powder, salt, and garlic powder together in a large bowl.
Add the warm water and olive oil. Stir until a soft dough forms, adding a splash of water if it feels dry.
Knead for 2 to 3 minutes, then let the dough rest for 10 minutes.
Divide the dough into six pieces and roll each piece into a thin round.
Heat a lightly oiled skillet over medium-high heat. Cook each flatbread for 2 to 3 minutes per side, until browned in spots and cooked through.
Brush the warm flatbreads with melted butter and sprinkle with optional parsley, Italian seasoning, or Parmesan.
Notes
A fast, no-yeast flatbread for nights when the bread basket has filed for bankruptcy.

title: Annette Freckles-Style Flour Tortillas
lines: Yield: 8 medium (7- to 8-inch) tortillas or 10 small (6- to 7-inch) tortillas | Serving size: 1 tortilla
Ingredients
1 1/2 cups all-purpose flour
1 teaspoon fine salt
1/4 cup avocado or olive oil, or melted butter
1/2 cup boiling water, plus 1 to 2 tablespoons only as needed
Directions
Whisk the all-purpose flour and salt together in a heatproof mixing bowl.
Add the oil or melted butter and mix until the flour is evenly coated and crumbly.
Slowly add 1/2 cup boiling water, stirring with a fork or sturdy spoon to avoid burns. Add more water 1 tablespoon at a time only if needed, until a soft, slightly tacky dough forms.
When the dough is cool enough to handle, knead for about 5 minutes, until smooth and no longer sticks heavily to your hands.
Cover the dough and let it rest for 15 to 20 minutes.

Divide into 8 equal balls for medium tortillas or 10 equal balls for small tortillas. Keep the balls covered while you work. Roll each one very thin: about 7 to 8 inches wide for 8 tortillas or 6 to 7 inches wide for 10.
Heat a dry skillet or comal over medium-high heat. Cook each tortilla for 20 to 30 seconds, until bubbles and light brown spots form. Flip and cook the second side for 20 to 30 seconds.
Stack the cooked tortillas in a clean kitchen towel to keep them soft and warm.
Notes
Add the water gradually; flour brands and humidity affect how much you need. Stop when the dough is soft and slightly tacky, rather than wet.
If the dough springs back while rolling, cover it and let it rest for another 5 to 10 minutes.
Oil makes the tortillas especially pliable; melted butter gives them a richer flavor.
Source
Adapted from Annette Freckles' oil-and-boiling-water tortilla method.

Heat a dry skillet or comal over medium-high heat. Cook each tortilla for 20 to 30 seconds, until bubbles and light brown spots form. Flip and cook the second side for 20 to 30 seconds.
Stack the cooked tortillas in a clean kitchen towel to keep them soft and warm.
Notes
Add the water gradually; flour brands and humidity affect how much you need. Stop when the dough is soft and slightly tacky, rather than wet.
If the dough springs back while rolling, cover it and let it rest for another 5 to 10 minutes.
Oil makes the tortillas especially pliable; melted butter gives them a richer flavor.

Adapted from Annette Freckles' oil-and-boiling-water tortilla method.

title: Incredible Banana Muffins
lines: Yield: 12 muffins | Serving size: 1 muffin
Ingredients
1 1/2 cups all-purpose flour
1 teaspoon baking powder
1 teaspoon baking soda
1/2 teaspoon salt
1 teaspoon ground cinnamon
1/4 teaspoon ground nutmeg
1 1/2 cups mashed very ripe bananas (about 3 large or 4 medium)
6 tablespoons butter, melted and cooled slightly
2/3 cup packed brown sugar (or 1/2 cup for less-sweet muffins)
1 large egg
1 teaspoon vanilla extract
2 tablespoons milk
Optional: 3/4 to 1 cup chopped walnuts or pecans
Directions
Preheat the oven to 425 degrees F. Grease or line a 12-cup muffin pan.
Whisk together the flour, baking powder, baking soda, salt, cinnamon, and nutmeg.
In a separate bowl, whisk the mashed bananas with the melted butter, brown sugar, egg, vanilla, and milk.
Add the dry ingredients and stir just until the flour disappears. Fold in the optional nuts.
Divide the batter among the muffin cups, filling them nearly to the top.
Bake at 425 degrees F for 5 minutes.
Without opening the oven, reduce the temperature to 350 degrees F and bake for another 16 to 18 minutes.
Remove when a toothpick comes out clean or with a few moist crumbs. Cool for 5 minutes in the pan, then transfer to a rack.

title: Banana White Chocolate Muffins
lines: Yield: 12 muffins | Serving size: 1 muffin
Ingredients
3 ripe bananas, mashed
3/4 cup white chocolate chips
1 1/2 cups all-purpose flour
1/2 cup packed brown sugar (light or dark)
4 1/2 tablespoons unsalted butter, melted
1 large egg plus 1 large egg yolk
3/4 teaspoon baking powder
3/4 teaspoon baking soda
3/8 teaspoon salt
1 teaspoon ground cinnamon
1 1/2 teaspoons vanilla extract
Directions
Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F. Grease or line a 12-cup muffin pan.
Whisk the flour, baking soda, baking powder, salt, and cinnamon together in a medium bowl.
In a separate large bowl, mix the mashed bananas, brown sugar, melted butter, egg, egg yolk, and vanilla until smooth.
Add the dry mixture to the wet mixture and stir gently just until combined. Do not overmix.
Fold in the white chocolate chips.
Fill each muffin cup about three-quarters full.
Bake for 18 to 22 minutes, until lightly golden and a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean.

title: Bakery-Style Boxed Yellow Cake Hack
lines: Yield: 16 small pieces | Serving size: 1 piece
Ingredients
1 box yellow or butter-recipe cake mix
4 large eggs
1/2 cup unsalted butter (1 stick), melted and cooled slightly
1 cup milk
1 to 2 teaspoons vanilla extract
Cooking spray or butter, for greasing the pan
1 tub Betty Crocker Hershey's chocolate frosting, about 16 ounces, optional
Directions
Preheat the oven to 315 degrees F. Grease a 9-by-11-inch baking pan.
Combine the cake mix, eggs, melted butter, milk, and vanilla until smooth. Use these amounts instead of the eggs, oil, and water listed on the box.
Pour the batter into the prepared pan and spread it evenly.
Bake for about 36 to 37 minutes, beginning the toothpick test around 32 minutes.
Cool the cake in the pan for 15 to 20 minutes.
If using frosting, microwave it for 15 seconds, stir, and continue in 5-to-10-second intervals just until pourable. Pour it over the cake, smooth the top, and let it set before serving.
Notes
Cake-mix sizes and ovens vary, so rely on the toothpick test rather than the clock alone.
A standard 9-by-13-inch pan may also be used; begin checking it several minutes earlier.
For a thicker frosting layer, cool the cake completely and spread the frosting without warming it.

title: Copycat Olive Garden Alfredo Sauce
lines: Yield: about 1 1/4 cups, 2 servings | Serving size: about 5/8 cup
Ingredients
2 tablespoons salted butter
1 teaspoon minced garlic
2 teaspoons all-purpose flour
1/2 cup heavy cream
1/2 cup whole milk
2 tablespoons plus 2 teaspoons finely grated Parmesan cheese
2 tablespoons plus 2 teaspoons finely grated Romano cheese
Salt and black pepper, to taste
Chopped fresh parsley, for garnish
Directions
Melt the butter in a saucepan over medium heat. Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Whisk in the flour and cook for 1 minute, stirring continuously.
Gradually whisk in the heavy cream, followed by the milk, adding each in small splashes to keep the sauce smooth.
Bring to a gentle bubble, then reduce the heat and simmer until slightly thickened.
Reduce the heat to low. Add the Parmesan and Romano gradually, stirring until melted and smooth.
Remove from the heat. Taste and adjust the salt and black pepper. Use while warm, adding a small splash of milk if the sauce becomes too thick.

title: Copycat Olive Garden Fettuccine Alfredo
lines: Yield: 2 hearty bowls | Serving size: 1/2 recipe
Ingredients
5 1/3 ounces dried fettuccine
1 batch Copycat Olive Garden Alfredo Sauce (about 1 1/4 cups)
Salt, for the pasta water
Chopped fresh parsley, for garnish
Directions
Bring a pot of salted water to a boil and cook the fettuccine according to the package directions until al dente.
Prepare the Alfredo sauce while the pasta cooks, or warm a previously prepared batch gently over low heat.
Reserve a small splash of pasta water, then drain the fettuccine.
Toss the hot fettuccine with the Alfredo sauce. Add a little reserved pasta water only if needed to loosen the sauce.
Divide evenly among bowls, garnish with parsley, and serve immediately.

title: Blended Caramelized Onion and Garlic Pasta
lines: Yield: 8 servings | Serving size: 1/8 of recipe
Ingredients
4 large onions, thinly sliced
4 tablespoons butter
1/2 cup extra-virgin olive oil
5 garlic cloves, minced
3 pasteurized egg yolks
3/4 cup finely grated Parmesan cheese
1 cup warm reserved pasta water, plus more as needed
Salt and black pepper, to taste
1 pound spaghetti or other pasta, cooked until al dente
Chopped fresh parsley, optional
Directions
Cook the pasta in salted water until al dente. Reserve at least 1 1/2 cups of the pasta water, then drain.

Meanwhile, melt the butter in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the onions and a pinch of salt. Cook for 25 to 40 minutes, stirring often and lowering the heat if needed, until deeply golden, soft, and jammy.
Stir in the 5 minced garlic cloves and cook for 1 minute, just until fragrant.
Carefully transfer the hot onion-garlic mixture to a heat-safe blender or food processor. If using a blender, vent the lid and cover the opening with a folded kitchen towel.
Add the olive oil, egg yolks, Parmesan, salt, and pepper. Blend until smooth, gradually adding up to 1 cup of warm pasta water to reach a velvety consistency.
Return the sauce to the skillet over low heat. Add the pasta and toss until evenly coated, adding more pasta water as needed.
Serve hot, garnished with parsley if desired.
Notes
Use pasteurized egg yolks because the sauce is warmed gently rather than fully cooked.
Caramelization time varies with the pan and heat; rely on the onions' deep color and jammy texture.
The sauce thickens as it stands. Loosen it with a splash of hot pasta water before serving.
Source
Adapted from Corey B's viral Blended Caramelized Onion Pasta Sauce.

title: Savory Creamy Tomato and Herb Pasta Sauce
lines: Yield: about 4 cups sauce, 4 servings | Serving size: about 1 cup sauce with 4 ounces dry pasta
Ingredients
1 pound penne or rigatoni
2 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil
1 tablespoon unsalted butter
1/2 cup yellow onion, very finely diced
1/2 cup carrot, very finely diced
1/2 cup celery, very finely diced
4 garlic cloves, minced
2 tablespoons tomato paste
1 teaspoon dried oregano
1/2 teaspoon dried thyme
1/2 teaspoon crushed red pepper flakes, optional
1/2 cup dry white wine or low-sodium chicken broth
4 cups cherry tomatoes, halved
1 teaspoon kosher salt, plus more for the pasta water and to taste
1/2 teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
3/4 cup heavy cream
3/4 cup finely grated Parmesan cheese, plus more for serving
1/2 cup reserved pasta water, as needed
1/4 cup chopped fresh basil
2 tablespoons chopped fresh parsley
Directions
Bring a large pot of well-salted water to a boil. Cook the pasta until 1 minute shy of al dente. Reserve the measured pasta water, then drain.
Heat the olive oil in a wide skillet or sauté pan over medium heat. Add the onion, carrot, and celery. Cook for 8 to 10 minutes, stirring often, until very soft but not browned.
Add the garlic, tomato paste, oregano, thyme, and optional red pepper flakes. Cook for 1 to 2 minutes, stirring constantly, until the tomato paste darkens slightly and smells rich.
Pour in the white wine or broth. Scrape up the browned bits and simmer for 2 to 3 minutes, until the liquid reduces by about half.
Add the cherry tomatoes, salt, and black pepper. Simmer uncovered for 12 to 15 minutes, stirring and gently crushing the tomatoes, until the vegetables melt into a thick sauce.
For a smoother restaurant-style finish, blend the sauce briefly with an immersion blender. Leave a few tomato pieces for texture.
Reduce the heat to low and stir in the heavy cream. Simmer gently for 3 to 5 minutes; do not let the sauce boil hard.
Stir in the Parmesan and butter until glossy. Add the drained pasta and toss over low heat, adding reserved pasta water a little at a time until the sauce clings to every piece.
Fold in the basil and parsley. Taste and adjust the salt, black pepper, or red pepper flakes. Serve with extra Parmesan.
Notes
Finely dicing the onion, carrot, and celery is what lets them nearly disappear into the sauce while building deep savory flavor.
White wine adds brightness; chicken broth gives a richer, alcohol-free finish.
Parmesan and broth vary in saltiness by brand, so make the final salt adjustment only after the cheese is added.
For sauce only, omit the pasta and reserve a little broth instead of pasta water for thinning.
Source
Flavor inspiration: Robert Irvine's Pasta Sauce; adapted into an original creamy cherry-tomato recipe for this collection.

title: Bulgarian-Style Kufteta Meat Patties
lines: Yield: about 8 small patties (4 servings) | Serving size: 2 patties | Prep: 15 minutes | Cook: 20 minutes
Ingredients
½ pound ground pork
½ pound ground beef
½ small yellow or white onion, very finely chopped
½ large egg, beaten (about 1 tablespoon plus 2 teaspoons)
½ cup finely shredded kashkaval, mild cheddar, or Monterey Jack cheese
2 tablespoons plus 2 teaspoons milk
1 teaspoon dried summer savory (Bulgarian chubritsa), optional but recommended
½ teaspoon ground cumin, optional
½ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
¾ teaspoon fine sea salt, plus more only after cooking a tester patty
1½ teaspoons chopped fresh parsley or ½ teaspoon dried parsley
1 teaspoon low-sodium soy sauce, optional
Neutral oil, as needed for the skillet
Directions
Prepare the Oven: Preheat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Line a rimmed baking sheet with foil or parchment paper and lightly grease it.

Mix the Meat: In a large bowl, combine the pork, beef, onion, egg, cheese, milk, summer savory, cumin, black pepper, salt, parsley, and soy sauce. Mix just until evenly combined; overmixing can make the patties firm.
Check the Seasoning: Cook a small tester patty completely, then taste it. Add a little more salt only if needed; never taste the raw mixture.
Shape: Wet or lightly oil your hands. Divide the mixture into 8 equal portions, roll each into a ball, and gently flatten it into a patty about 1/2 inch thick.

Brown the Patties: Heat a thin layer of neutral oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Working in batches, brown the patties for 2 to 3 minutes per side, then transfer them to the prepared baking sheet.
Finish in the Oven: Bake for 8 to 10 minutes, or until the center of the thickest patty reaches 160°F (71°C). Let the patties rest for 3 minutes.
Serve: Enjoy hot with a crisp salad, roasted vegetables, potatoes, rice, or fries.

Meatloaf option: Use the same ingredient mixture. Heat the oven to 350°F. Skip skillet browning and shape into a compact loaf about 2 inches thick on a lined, lightly greased rimmed baking sheet. For the 1-pound master batch (4 servings), make a loaf about 7 by 4 inches and bake for about 40–55 minutes, checking at 35 minutes, until the center reaches 160°F. For scaled batches, adjust loaf length and begin checking smaller loaves earlier; the center temperature determines doneness. Rest for 10 minutes before slicing into 4 equal servings.
Notes
Summer savory, called chubritsa in Bulgarian cooking, gives kufteta their characteristic herbal flavor.
Cheese and soy sauce vary in saltiness, so begin with the listed salt and use the tester patty before adding more.
This pork-and-beef mixture must reach 160°F (71°C) in the center of every patty.
Source
Adapted from Emma & Is Kitchen — Kufteta: Traditional Bulgarian Meatball Recipe
Food-safety reference: USDA — Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart

title: Bulgarian Stuffed Grape Leaves (Lozovi Sarmi)
lines: Yield: about 60 rolls (6 servings) | Serving size: about 10 rolls | Prep: 40 minutes | Cook: 45–50 minutes
Ingredients
60 grape leaves, fresh or jarred in brine (leaf size and package count vary by brand)
1 pound ground beef, ground pork, or a 50/50 mixture
1 cup uncooked medium-grain white rice, rinsed and thoroughly drained
1 medium yellow onion (or 1 cup), finely chopped
2 medium tomatoes, grated or finely chopped, or 1/2 cup smooth tomato purée
2 tablespoons olive oil or neutral vegetable oil
1 tablespoon chopped fresh parsley
1 teaspoon dried summer savory (Bulgarian chubritsa)
1 teaspoon fine sea salt, using less if the leaves are salty
1/2 teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
2 cups water, divided equally, plus more if needed
Plain whole-milk yogurt, for serving
Directions

Prepare the Leaves: If using jarred leaves, drain and gently separate them, rinse well under cool water, and trim any thick stems; blanch for 1 minute only if they remain stiff. If using fresh leaves, trim the stems and blanch in simmering water for 2 to 3 minutes until pliable. Drain and let cool.

Make the Filling: Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat. Cook the onion for 4 to 5 minutes until softened. Add the ground meat and cook until browned, breaking it into small crumbles. Stir in the tomatoes and cook for 1 to 2 minutes. Add the rice and cook for 1 minute.

Partially Cook the Rice: Pour in half of the measured water. Reduce the heat and simmer uncovered for about 5 to 8 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the liquid is absorbed. Stir in the parsley, summer savory, salt, and black pepper. Remove from the heat and cool until comfortable to handle.

Fill and Roll: Lay each leaf shiny side down with the veins facing up and the stem end toward you. Place 1 to 2 teaspoons filling near the stem end. Fold the bottom over the filling, tuck in both sides, and roll snugly but not tightly—the rice needs room to expand. Make about 60 rolls; overlap two leaves if one is torn.
Arrange the Sarmi: Line the bottom of a heavy pot with any damaged or extra leaves. Arrange the rolls seam-side down in snug layers so they cannot unravel.
Add the Weight and Liquid: Pour the remaining measured water around the rolls. Set a small heatproof plate upside down directly on top to keep them submerged, then cover the pot.

Simmer: Bring the liquid just to a simmer over medium heat, then reduce to low. Cook gently for 40 to 50 minutes, adding a splash of hot water if the pot becomes dry, until the leaves and rice are tender and the filling is fully cooked.
Rest and Serve: Carefully remove the hot plate. Let the sarmi rest, covered, for 10 minutes, then serve warm with plain yogurt.
Notes
Do not overfill or roll the leaves too tightly; the rice expands as it cooks.
Jarred grape leaves can be quite salty. Rinse them thoroughly and reduce the added salt if needed.
For beef, pork, or a beef-and-pork blend, cook the filling to at least 160°F (71°C). If using ground chicken or turkey, cook it to 165°F (74°C).
Leaf size and the number of usable leaves per jar vary by brand, so keep a few extras nearby.
Source
Adapted from Daniela at Taco & Tiramisu — Lozovi Sarmi: Stuffed Grape Leaves
Food-safety reference: USDA — Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart

2/3 medium tomato, grated or finely chopped, or 2 tablespoons plus 2 teaspoons smooth tomato purée
2 teaspoons olive oil or neutral vegetable oil
1 teaspoon chopped fresh parsley
1/3 teaspoon dried summer savory (Bulgarian chubritsa)
1/3 teaspoon fine sea salt, using less if the leaves are salty
1/8 teaspoon plus a pinch freshly ground black pepper
2/3 cup water, divided equally, plus more if needed
Plain whole-milk yogurt, for serving
Directions

Prepare the Leaves: If using jarred leaves, drain and gently separate them, rinse well under cool water, and trim any thick stems; blanch for 1 minute only if they remain stiff. If using fresh leaves, trim the stems and blanch in simmering water for 2 to 3 minutes until pliable. Drain and let cool.

Make the Filling: Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat. Cook the onion for 4 to 5 minutes until softened. Add the ground meat and cook until browned, breaking it into small crumbles. Stir in the tomatoes and cook for 1 to 2 minutes. Add the rice and cook for 1 minute.

Partially Cook the Rice: Pour in half of the measured water. Reduce the heat and simmer uncovered for about 5 to 8 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the liquid is absorbed. Stir in the parsley, summer savory, salt, and black pepper. Remove from the heat and cool until comfortable to handle.

Fill and Roll: Lay each leaf shiny side down with the veins facing up and the stem end toward you. Place 1 to 2 teaspoons filling near the stem end. Fold the bottom over the filling, tuck in both sides, and roll snugly but not tightly—the rice needs room to expand. Make about 20 rolls; overlap two leaves if one is torn.
Arrange the Sarmi: Line the bottom of a heavy pot with any damaged or extra leaves. Arrange the rolls seam-side down in snug layers so they cannot unravel.
Add the Weight and Liquid: Pour the remaining measured water around the rolls. Set a small heatproof plate upside down directly on top to keep them submerged, then cover the pot.

Simmer: Bring the liquid just to a simmer over medium heat, then reduce to low. Cook gently for 40 to 50 minutes, adding a splash of hot water if the pot becomes dry, until the leaves and rice are tender and the filling is fully cooked.
Rest and Serve: Carefully remove the hot plate. Let the sarmi rest, covered, for 10 minutes, then serve warm with plain yogurt.
Notes
Do not overfill or roll the leaves too tightly; the rice expands as it cooks.
Jarred grape leaves can be quite salty. Rinse them thoroughly and reduce the added salt if needed.
For beef, pork, or a beef-and-pork blend, cook the filling to at least 160°F (71°C). If using ground chicken or turkey, cook it to 165°F (74°C).
Leaf size and the number of usable leaves per jar vary by brand, so keep a few extras nearby.

title: Alice Springs Chicken (Outback Copycat)
lines: Yield: 6 servings | Prep: 15 minutes | Cook: 25–35 minutes
Ingredients
6 boneless, skinless chicken breasts
6 slices cooked bacon, chopped
1 cup sliced mushrooms
1 cup shredded cheddar
½ cup mayonnaise
¼ cup honey
2 tablespoons Dijon mustard
1 tablespoon lemon juice
Salt and black pepper, to taste
Oil or butter, as needed for the skillet
Directions
Heat the oven to 400°F (205°C). Pat the chicken dry and pound to an even thickness; season with salt and pepper.
Mix the mayonnaise, honey, Dijon, and lemon juice. Reserve half in a clean bowl for serving.
Sauté the mushrooms in a little oil or butter until browned; set aside. Brown the chicken in the skillet for 3 to 4 minutes per side.
Transfer to a baking dish. Spread the remaining sauce over the chicken, then add the mushrooms, cooked bacon, and cheddar.
Bake for about 10 to 20 minutes, until the thickest part reaches 165°F (74°C). Serve with the reserved clean sauce.
Notes
Image ingredient amounts retained. Method adapted for those amounts; this is a copycat, not an official Outback recipe.
Each serving is 1 chicken breast with one-sixth of the toppings. Chicken weights assume six 6-ounce breasts; actual sizes vary.
Source
Ingredient source: Corey’s supplied Easy Steps Recipes image. Directions developed for these quantities; related published recipe: https://www.culinaryhill.com/alice-springs-chicken-outback-copycat/

title: Melt in Your Mouth Parmesan Chicken
lines: Yield: 6 servings | Prep: 10 minutes | Bake: 25–45 minutes
Ingredients
6 boneless, skinless chicken breasts
1 cup mayonnaise
1 cup grated Parmesan
1 teaspoon garlic powder
1 teaspoon onion powder
1 teaspoon dried thyme
½ teaspoon salt
½ teaspoon black pepper
½ cup seasoned breadcrumbs
Directions
Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C). Lightly grease a baking dish. Pound the chicken to an even thickness and arrange in a single layer.
Combine mayonnaise, Parmesan, garlic powder, onion powder, thyme, salt, and pepper. Spread over the chicken.
Sprinkle evenly with breadcrumbs. Bake uncovered for about 25 to 45 minutes, depending on thickness, until the chicken reaches 165°F (74°C).
If needed, briefly broil to brown the topping, watching closely. Rest 5 minutes before serving.
Notes
Ingredients follow the supplied image; directions are developed for that version using the linked recipe as a method reference.
Serving size: 1 breast with one-sixth of the coating. Start checking thin breasts early.

lines: Yield: 6 servings | Prep: 10 minutes | Bake: about 40–50 minutes
Ingredients

title: Buttermilk Fried Chicken
lines: Yield: 6 servings | Prep: 20 minutes | Marinate: 6 hours | Fry: about 25–35 minutes per batch
Ingredients
6 bone-in chicken pieces (or 6–8 mixed pieces for the full batch)
2 cups buttermilk
2 cups all-purpose flour
1 tablespoon salt
1 teaspoon black pepper
1 teaspoon paprika
1 teaspoon garlic powder
½ teaspoon onion powder
½ teaspoon cayenne pepper
Vegetable oil, enough for a 1½- to 2-inch depth in a heavy frying pot; do not scale oil strictly by servings
Directions
Cover chicken with buttermilk and refrigerate for 6 hours.

Mix flour with the salt, black pepper, paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, and cayenne. Lift chicken from the buttermilk, let excess drip off, and coat thoroughly in seasoned flour. Rest on a rack for 10 minutes.
Heat the oil to about 350°F (175°C) in a heavy pot, leaving ample space above the oil. Fry in uncrowded batches, turning carefully; maintain about 325°F (163°C) while cooking.
Cook until crisp and the thickest part of every piece reaches 165°F (74°C), usually 25 to 35 minutes for bone-in pieces. If the crust browns first, finish on a rack in a 350°F oven.
Drain on a rack. Discard leftover raw-chicken marinade and flour.
Notes

The image calls this Chef John’s, but his published recipe uses a different herb and spice blend. This entry preserves the image’s simpler ingredients; the source link points to his original for comparison.
Full batch: 6 servings, divide the 6–8 pieces among six people. Serving tabs use about 9 ounces bone-in chicken per person; piece size and coating use vary.
Frying oil depth and pan capacity determine the amount needed. Allow oil to recover between batches.
Source

Ingredient source: Corey’s supplied Easy Steps Recipes image. Directions developed for these quantities; related published recipe: https://www.allrecipes.com/recipe/220128/chef-johns-buttermilk-fried-chicken/

title: Creamy Chicken and Stuffing Bake
lines: Yield: 6 servings | Prep: 15 minutes | Bake: about 35–45 minutes
Ingredients
4 boneless, skinless chicken breasts
6 ounces dry stuffing mix
10.5 ounces condensed cream of chicken soup
½ cup sour cream
½ cup chicken broth
¼ cup melted butter
½ teaspoon garlic powder
½ teaspoon onion powder
½ teaspoon dried thyme
Salt and black pepper, to taste
Additional hot water or broth, as required by the stuffing package
Directions

Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C). Grease a baking dish. Cut the chicken into six comparable portions for the full batch, or use the listed weight in the serving tabs. Season with garlic powder, onion powder, thyme, salt, and pepper.
Mix the condensed soup and sour cream. Arrange the chicken in the dish and spread this mixture over it.

Moisten the stuffing with the listed broth and melted butter. Add enough hot water or broth to meet the package’s liquid directions; the image’s ½ cup broth alone may be insufficient. Spread over the chicken.
Cover with foil and bake for 25 minutes. Uncover and bake about 10 to 20 minutes more, until the center of the chicken and stuffing reaches 165°F (74°C). Rest 5 minutes.
Notes
Image quantities retained, with extra liquid allowed to properly hydrate the stuffing. Package directions and sodium levels vary by brand.
Full batch serves 6, despite using 4 breasts. Divide the finished casserole into six equal portions. Chicken weight assumes about 2 pounds total.
Linked manufacturer recipe supports the layering method; its exact ingredients differ from this .
Source

Ingredient source: Corey’s supplied Easy Steps Recipes image. Directions developed for these quantities; related published recipe: https://www.kraftheinz.com/stove-top/recipes/501776-stove-top-one-dish-chicken-bake

title: French Onion Chicken Breast Bake
lines: Yield: 6 servings | Prep: 15 minutes | Caramelize onions: 30–45 minutes | Bake: about 20–30 minutes
Ingredients
6 boneless, skinless chicken breasts
2 large onions, thinly sliced
2 tablespoons butter
1 cup beef broth
1 teaspoon Worcestershire sauce
1 cup shredded Swiss cheese
½ cup shredded Parmesan
1 teaspoon garlic powder
½ teaspoon dried thyme
Salt and black pepper, to taste
Directions

Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C). Melt the butter in a skillet over medium-low heat. Add onions and cook for 30 to 45 minutes, stirring often, until deeply golden. Add a little of the measured broth if they stick.
Stir in the remaining broth, Worcestershire, and thyme; simmer for 3 to 5 minutes.
Pound chicken to an even thickness and season with garlic powder, salt, and pepper. Arrange in a baking dish and spoon the onions and broth around and over it.
Bake about 20 to 30 minutes, until the thickest part reaches 165°F (74°C). Add Swiss and Parmesan during the final 5 minutes to melt. Rest 5 minutes.
If desired, briefly broil the cheese while watching closely.
Notes
Image ingredient amounts retained; the linked recipe is a related caramelized-onion chicken reference.
Serving size: 1 breast with one-sixth of the onion sauce and cheese. The image’s 35 minutes does not include sufficient time for deeply caramelized onions.

title: Crockpot Mississippi Meatballs
lines: Yield: 6 servings | LOW: about 4–6 hours, following meatball package directions
Ingredients
2 pounds fully cooked frozen beef meatballs
1 packet ranch seasoning mix (brand or size dependent)
1 packet au jus gravy mix (brand or size dependent)
½ cup unsalted butter
6 to 8 pepperoncini peppers (brand or size dependent)
½ cup pepperoncini juice
Directions
Use fully cooked meatballs whose package permits slow cooking from frozen. If the package requires thawing, thaw in the refrigerator first.
Place meatballs in the slow cooker. Sprinkle with the ranch and au jus mixes. Add pepperoncini juice, peppers, and butter cut into pieces.
Cover and cook on LOW for about 4 to 6 hours, or according to the package’s slow-cooker directions, until the centers are thoroughly hot. Stir gently once during cooking.
Stir the melted butter into the sauce and divide into equal portions. Serve with potatoes, rice, or noodles if desired.
Notes
Ingredient amounts come from Corey’s supplied Easy Steps Recipes image. Exact published directions could not be verified; the cooking method here was developed for the pictured ingredients.

Packet sizes and salt levels vary. No additional broth is included in the image; if your cooker requires more liquid, follow its instructions and record any added amount. The image’s 4-hour time is an estimate.

Divide the finished batch evenly among the listed servings. Meat and produce weights are approximate. Packet weights and seasoning strength depend on the brand. Mix packet contents thoroughly before measuring a fractional amount.

Use a slow cooker sized for the batch and follow its manufacturer’s fill guidance. A 1-person batch may be too small for a standard cooker; use an appropriately sized model or prepare the larger batch. Do not reduce cooking time in direct proportion to servings.

title: Slow Cooker Chicken and Potatoes
lines: Yield: 6 servings | LOW: about 5–6 hours; check for doneness
Ingredients
4 boneless, skinless chicken thighs
1.5 pounds baby potatoes, halved
4 carrots, sliced
1 small onion, chopped
3 garlic cloves, minced
1 cup chicken broth
1 teaspoon Italian seasoning
Salt and black pepper, to taste
Directions
Use thawed chicken. Cut potatoes into evenly sized halves or quarters and slice carrots about ¼ inch thick.
Put potatoes, carrots, onion, and garlic in the slow cooker. Add broth and Italian seasoning. Season chicken with salt and pepper and arrange over the vegetables.
Cover and cook on LOW for about 5 to 6 hours. Check that chicken reaches 165°F (74°C) and vegetables are fork-tender.
If chicken finishes first, remove it and keep warm while vegetables finish. Divide chicken and vegetables evenly among the servings.

title: Slow Cooker Chicken and Gravy
lines: Yield: 6 servings | LOW: about 4–6 hours; check chicken temperature
Ingredients
4 boneless, skinless chicken breasts
1 packet ranch seasoning mix (brand or size dependent)
1 packet brown gravy mix (brand or size dependent)
1 cup chicken broth
½ cup sour cream
½ teaspoon garlic powder
½ teaspoon onion powder
Salt and black pepper, to taste
Directions
Whisk broth, ranch mix, brown gravy mix, garlic powder, and onion powder in the slow cooker.
Add thawed chicken and turn to coat. Cover and cook on LOW for about 4 to 6 hours, until chicken reaches 165°F (74°C) and shreds easily.
Remove chicken and shred with two forks. Turn the cooker to WARM.
Mix a few spoonfuls of hot cooking liquid into the sour cream, then stir it into the gravy. Return shredded chicken and stir until warm. Taste before adding salt and pepper.

title: Slow Cooker Beef and Broccoli
lines: Yield: 6 servings | LOW: about 4–6 hours, plus 20–40 minutes to finish
Ingredients
2 pounds beef chuck roast, thinly sliced across the grain
4 cups broccoli florets
½ cup soy sauce
¼ cup packed brown sugar
3 garlic cloves, minced
1 tablespoon minced fresh ginger
2 tablespoons cornstarch
¼ cup cold water, for slurry
Directions
Place sliced beef in the slow cooker. Mix soy sauce, brown sugar, garlic, and ginger, then pour over the beef and toss.
Cover and cook on LOW for about 4 to 6 hours, until tender. Check occasionally toward the end; thin slices may finish earlier.
Mix cornstarch with the listed cold water. Stir into the hot beef sauce. Switch to HIGH and cook for about 15 to 20 minutes, until thickened.
Add broccoli for the final 20 to 40 minutes, cooking until just tender. Alternatively, steam broccoli separately and fold into the finished beef.
Notes
Ingredient amounts come from Corey’s supplied Easy Steps Recipes image. Exact published directions could not be verified; the cooking method here was developed for the pictured ingredients.

The image includes no broth and reserves all ¼ cup water for the slurry. If your cooker needs more starting liquid, follow its instructions; any added broth or water is an adaptation. Keep broccoli out of the initial long cook.

title: Slow Cooker Chicken and Dumplings
lines: Yield: 6 servings | LOW: about 4–6 hours, then HIGH: about 1–1½ hours
Ingredients
4 boneless, skinless chicken breasts
10.5 ounces condensed cream of chicken soup
1 cup chicken broth
2 cups frozen mixed vegetables
16.3 ounces refrigerated biscuit dough
½ teaspoon garlic powder
½ teaspoon onion powder
Salt and black pepper, to taste
Directions
Whisk soup, broth, garlic powder, onion powder, salt, and pepper in the slow cooker. Add thawed chicken.
Cover and cook on LOW for about 4 to 6 hours, until chicken reaches 165°F (74°C) and shreds easily. Shred and return to the pot.
Stir in mixed vegetables and switch to HIGH. Let the mixture become hot and gently bubbling before adding dough.

Cut biscuits into small pieces. Arrange over the hot filling in a loose layer, pressing them slightly into the liquid. Cover and cook on HIGH for about 60 to 90 minutes without repeatedly lifting the lid.
Split a dumpling to check the center: it should be cooked through, fluffy, and free of raw, gummy dough. Continue cooking if needed, then serve.
Notes
Ingredient amounts come from Corey’s supplied Easy Steps Recipes image. Exact published directions could not be verified; the cooking method here was developed for the pictured ingredients.

The image’s 6-hour time does not reliably account for cooking biscuit dumplings. Brand, dough thickness, and cooker temperature affect the finishing time. Follow biscuit-package food-safety instructions; do not serve raw dough.

25 ounces refrigerated cheese ravioli
24 ounces marinara sauce
1 cup crushed tomatoes
½ cup chicken broth
1 teaspoon Italian seasoning
2 garlic cloves, minced
1 cup shredded mozzarella
Directions
If using raw Italian sausage, brown and cook the links through in a skillet before slicing; cook pork sausage to 160°F (71°C), or poultry sausage to 165°F (74°C). Drain excess fat.
Combine cooked sliced sausage, marinara, crushed tomatoes, broth, Italian seasoning, and garlic in the slow cooker.
Cover and cook on LOW for about 3 hours, until hot and flavors have blended.

Stir in refrigerated ravioli. Cover and cook on HIGH, checking after 30 minutes and then every 15 minutes, until the pasta and filling are fully cooked according to the package. Thin fresh ravioli may cook sooner.
Sprinkle mozzarella over the top. Cover for 10 to 15 minutes to melt, then serve.
Notes
Ingredient amounts come from Corey’s supplied Easy Steps Recipes image. Exact published directions could not be verified; the cooking method here was developed for the pictured ingredients.

Refrigerated ravioli is added near the end to limit splitting and mushiness; this is a developed method, not verified original directions. The photo’s browned cheese would require a separate oven-safe broiling step; never put a standard slow-cooker insert under a broiler unless its manufacturer explicitly permits it.

Divide the finished batch evenly among the listed servings. Meat and produce weights are approximate. Packet weights and seasoning strength depend on the brand. Mix packet contents thoroughly before measuring a fractional amount.

Use a slow cooker sized for the batch and follow its manufacturer’s fill guidance. A 1-person batch may be too small for a standard cooker; use an appropriately sized model or prepare the larger batch. Do not reduce cooking time in direct proportion to servings.

title: Slow Cooker Cowboy Casserole
lines: Estimated yield: 6 servings | Divide finished batch evenly
Ingredients
1 pound lean ground beef
1 cup chopped onion
1 tablespoon minced garlic
16 ounces canned kidney beans, drained and rinsed
14.5 ounces canned tomatoes with juice
10 ounces diced tomatoes with fire-roasted hatch chiles
1 cup frozen corn
1 teaspoon kosher salt (size or brand dependent)
½ teaspoon black pepper
¼ teaspoon chipotle powder
1.5 pounds Yukon Gold potatoes, thinly sliced
1¼ cups shredded Colby and Monterey Jack cheese
Directions
Brown beef with onion in a skillet; drain. Add garlic and cook 30 seconds.
Layer potatoes, beef, canned tomatoes, drained canned beans, corn, and seasonings in the cooker. Stir gently.
Cook covered on LOW about 6–7 hours until potatoes are tender. Sprinkle with cheese and cover 10–15 minutes to melt. Divide into 6 portions.

1 teaspoon black pepper

title: Slow Cooker Cottage Cheese Lasagna
lines: Estimated yield: 6 servings | Divide finished batch evenly
Ingredients
1.5 pounds ground beef
2 tablespoons Italian seasoning
24 ounces roasted garlic herb spaghetti sauce
2½ cups shredded mozzarella
2½ cups small-curd cottage cheese
1 large egg, beaten
12 regular dry lasagna noodles
1 cup beef broth
Chopped fresh parsley, to taste
Directions
Brown beef in a skillet and drain. Stir in sauce, broth, and Italian seasoning. Mix cottage cheese with beaten egg and parsley separately.
Spread a little meat sauce in a greased cooker. Layer broken dry noodles, meat sauce, cottage-cheese mixture, and mozzarella; repeat, finishing with sauce. Reserve some mozzarella for the finish.
Cook covered on LOW about 3½–4½ hours until noodles are tender and the center reaches 165°F. Add reserved cheese for the last 15 minutes. Rest 20 minutes before dividing into 6 servings.

title: Slow Cooker Cheesy Spaghetti
lines: Estimated yield: 6 servings | Divide finished batch evenly
Ingredients
1 tablespoon olive oil
1 pound lean ground beef
½ cup diced onion
1 tablespoon minced garlic
2 teaspoons Italian seasoning
½ teaspoon salt
¼ teaspoon black pepper
1 pound dry spaghetti
48 ounces tomato and basil marinara
15 ounces crushed tomatoes
2 cups chicken broth
½ cup grated Parmesan
1½ cups shredded mozzarella
1 tablespoon chopped parsley
Directions
Heat oil in a skillet; brown beef and onion, drain, then stir in garlic for 30 seconds.
Place beef, marinara, crushed tomatoes, broth, Italian seasoning, salt, and pepper in the cooker. Cover and cook on LOW for 3–4 hours.

Break dry spaghetti in half and submerge in the hot sauce. Cook on HIGH about 30–60 minutes, stirring every 15 minutes, until tender. Add a splash of hot water if sauce becomes dry before pasta cooks.
Stir in Parmesan. Top with mozzarella, cover until melted, and finish with parsley. Divide into 6 portions.

title: Slow Cooker Three-Cheese Macaroni
lines: Estimated yield: 6 servings | Divide finished batch evenly
Ingredients

4 cups whole milk
8 ounces yellow cheddar, freshly shredded
8 ounces white cheddar, freshly shredded
8 ounces Velveeta, cubed
1½ teaspoons sea salt
½ teaspoon white pepper
1 teaspoon ground mustard
Directions
Parboil macaroni for about 4 minutes, then drain. This added preparation helps the pasta cook evenly.
Grease the cooker. Add warm milk, cheeses, salt, pepper, mustard, and pasta. Stir.
Cook on LOW about 1–2 hours, stirring every 20–30 minutes, until pasta is tender and cheese is melted. Stop cooking promptly; thin with a splash of warm milk if needed. Do not use HIGH.
Divide into 6 main-dish portions or 8–10 side portions.

title: Slow Cooker Marry Me Chicken
lines: Estimated yield: 6 servings | Divide finished batch evenly
Ingredients
1.5 pounds chicken breast
1 teaspoon salt
1 teaspoon black pepper
1 tablespoon olive oil
4 garlic cloves, minced
1 cup chicken broth
½ cup heavy cream
2 tablespoons cornstarch
½ cup chopped sun-dried tomatoes, drained
4 sprigs fresh thyme (size or brand dependent)
½ teaspoon red pepper flakes
¼ cup grated Parmesan
8 fresh basil leaves, sliced
2 tablespoons cold water, for slurry (added clarification)
Directions
Season thawed chicken with salt and pepper. Brown briefly in olive oil in a skillet, then transfer to the cooker. Add garlic, broth, sun-dried tomatoes, thyme, and pepper flakes.
Cook covered on LOW about 3–5 hours until chicken reaches 165°F. Remove thyme stems.

Whisk cornstarch with the listed cold water. Stir into the hot sauce and cook on HIGH about 15–20 minutes until thickened. Reduce heat and stir in cream and Parmesan. Warm gently, finish with basil, and divide into 6 portions.

title: Slow Cooker Creamy Butter Chicken
lines: Estimated yield: 6 servings | Divide finished batch evenly
Ingredients
3 pounds chicken breasts, cubed
1 cup chopped onion
4 tablespoons unsalted butter
1 cup tomato sauce
1½ cups heavy cream
6 tablespoons tomato paste
1 tablespoon minced garlic
1 tablespoon grated ginger
2½ teaspoons curry powder
2 teaspoons chili powder
2 teaspoons garam masala
½ teaspoon cumin
¾ teaspoon salt
2 tablespoons cornstarch
2 tablespoons cold water, for slurry (added clarification)
4 cups cooked jasmine rice, optional
Fresh cilantro, for serving
Directions
Soften onion in butter in a skillet. Add garlic, ginger, curry powder, chili powder, garam masala, and cumin; stir for 30 seconds.
Transfer to the cooker with thawed chicken, tomato sauce, tomato paste, and salt. Cover and cook on LOW about 4–6 hours, until chicken reaches 165°F.
Mix cornstarch with cold water, stir into the hot sauce, and cook on HIGH about 15–20 minutes to thicken. Reduce heat; stir in cream and warm gently.
Divide into 6 portions. Serve with the optional cooked rice and cilantro.

title: Slow Cooker Creamy Garlic Beef
lines: Yield: 6 servings | LOW: about 6–8 hours, plus 20–30 minutes to finish
Ingredients
2 pounds beef chuck, cut into 1½-inch cubes
1 cup beef broth
8 ounces cremini mushrooms, sliced
6 garlic cloves, minced
1 cup heavy cream
2 tablespoons butter
1 teaspoon dried thyme
2 tablespoons cornstarch
2 tablespoons cold water, for cornstarch slurry (added clarification)
Salt and black pepper, optional, to taste (added seasoning option)
Directions
Melt butter in a skillet over medium-high heat. Pat the thawed beef dry and brown in batches. Transfer beef to the slow cooker. Browning adds flavor but is not required for the long cook.
Add mushrooms and garlic to the skillet; stir briefly. Pour in the broth and scrape up the browned bits. Transfer everything to the cooker and add thyme.
Cover and cook on LOW for about 6–8 hours, until beef is fork-tender. Do not add the cream yet.
Mix cornstarch with the listed cold water. Stir into the hot cooking liquid. Cover and cook on HIGH for about 15–20 minutes, until thickened.
Reduce the heat to LOW or WARM. Stir in heavy cream and gently heat through without boiling. Taste and season if desired. Divide into the listed portions.
Notes
The photo suggests browned beef and a reduced sauce; browning is included as an optional flavor step. Add cream at the end to limit separation.

title: Slow Cooker Chicken Parmesan
lines: Yield: 6 servings | LOW: about 4–6 hours; check chicken early
Ingredients
2 pounds boneless, skinless chicken breasts
24 ounces marinara sauce
1 teaspoon Italian seasoning
1 cup shredded mozzarella
½ cup grated Parmesan
2 garlic cloves, minced
½ teaspoon black pepper
Directions
Use thawed chicken. Cut very large breasts into comparable portions so they cook evenly.
Mix marinara, garlic, Italian seasoning, and pepper in the cooker. Add chicken and spoon sauce over it.
Cover and cook on LOW for about 4–6 hours, checking earlier for thin pieces. Cook until the thickest part reaches 165°F (74°C).
Sprinkle mozzarella and Parmesan over the chicken. Cover for about 10–15 minutes, just until cheese melts. Serve the chicken and sauce in equal portions.
Notes
This is an unbreaded chicken Parmesan. The slow cooker melts cheese but does not create an oven-browned crust. Pasta or bread, if served alongside, is extra.

lines: Yield: 6 servings | LOW: about 6–8 hours, plus 20–30 minutes to finish
Ingredients

8 ounces mushrooms, sliced

0.33 pounds beef chuck, cut into 1½-inch cubes
1.33 ounces mushrooms, sliced
1/3 cup beef broth
0.17 medium onion, sliced
0.33 garlic cloves, minced
2 tablespoons plus 2 teaspoons sour cream
1 teaspoon Worcestershire sauce
1 teaspoon cornstarch
1 teaspoon cold water, for cornstarch slurry (added clarification)
Salt and black pepper, optional, to taste (added seasoning option)
Directions
Place thawed beef, mushrooms, onion, garlic, broth, and Worcestershire in the slow cooker. Stir to combine.
Cover and cook on LOW for about 6–8 hours until beef is fork-tender.
Mix cornstarch with the listed cold water. Stir into the hot liquid, switch to HIGH, and cook covered for about 15–20 minutes until thickened.
Turn off the heat. Whisk a few spoonfuls of hot sauce into the sour cream, then gently stir that mixture back into the cooker. Do not boil after adding sour cream.
Taste and season if desired. Divide into equal portions; serve over separately cooked egg noodles, rice, or potatoes if desired.
Notes
Sour cream goes in after cooking to reduce curdling. The pictured sauce may be thicker than the initial broth; allow the slurry time to thicken. Noodles are not included in the ingredient amounts.

title: Slow Cooker Cowboy Beans and Sausage
lines: Yield: 6 servings | LOW: about 4–6 hours
Ingredients
1 pound fully cooked smoked sausage, sliced
30 ounces canned pinto beans (two 15-ounce cans), drained
15 ounces canned kidney beans (one 15-ounce can), drained
1 cup barbecue sauce
½ cup beef broth
½ cup diced onion
2 tablespoons packed brown sugar
1 teaspoon smoked paprika
Salt and black pepper, optional, to taste (added seasoning option)
Directions
Use fully cooked smoked sausage and canned beans. Drain the beans. Slice sausage into even rounds.
Combine sausage, pinto beans, kidney beans, barbecue sauce, broth, onion, brown sugar, and smoked paprika in the cooker.
Cover and cook on LOW for about 4–6 hours, until onion is tender and the mixture is hot throughout. Stir gently toward the end.
If the sauce is thinner than desired, cook briefly uncovered on HIGH, stirring and watching it closely. Divide evenly among the listed servings.
Notes

Bean package weights refer to the labeled contents before draining; the drained yield varies by brand. Use canned beans as pictured. Dried kidney beans cannot be substituted directly into this slow-cooker method.

title: French Onion Meatloaf
lines: Yield: 1 loaf using 1 pound beef | 3 servings | Prep: 15 minutes, plus prepared toppings | Bake: about 40–55 minutes | Rest: 10 minutes
Ingredients
1 pound ground beef
0.5 packet French onion soup mix (packet weight varies by brand)
½ cup dry breadcrumbs
1 large egg
¼ cup milk
2 tablespoons ketchup
½ cup prepared caramelized onions
¾ cup shredded Swiss cheese
Directions
Prepare: Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Line a rimmed baking sheet with parchment or foil, or lightly grease a small baking dish. Use a pan that leaves room around the loaf.
Mix breadcrumbs, milk, egg, and soup mix in a bowl; stand 5 minutes. Gently combine with beef. Reserve ketchup, onions, and Swiss for topping.

Shape: Form gently into a compact loaf about 2–2½ inches thick. For the Master 1-pound beef batch, aim for roughly 7 by 4 inches. For serving-tab amounts, keep a similar thickness and adjust length, or make individual mini loaves.
Spread ketchup over the loaf before baking. After about 30 minutes, top with prepared caramelized onions. Add Swiss for the final 5–10 minutes, until melted.

Bake and Check: A loaf using 1 pound beef generally takes about 40–55 minutes at 350°F; topping and pan shape affect timing. Begin checking mini loaves after 20–25 minutes. Bake until a food thermometer in the center of the beef registers 160°F (71°C). Do not rely on color or the image’s full-batch time.
Rest and Slice: Carefully drain excess fat if needed. Rest for 10 minutes, then divide into the listed number of equal servings.
Notes
The listed caramelized onions are already cooked. If making them from raw onions, allow additional preparation time; cook sliced onions slowly until golden and cool before using.

Ingredients were transcribed from Corey’s supplied RecipesCrave image and halved from 2 pounds to 1 pound ground beef. Directions were developed for this version; they are not verified original publisher directions.

The original image lists 6 servings, so the halved Master batch is 3 servings. Serving tabs scale from that base. For fractional eggs, beat a whole egg, measure its total volume, and use the listed fraction.
Mix soup seasoning thoroughly before portioning it. Package salt levels vary; taste only a small cooked tester patty if adjusting seasoning.

title: Cheesy Baked Parmesan Meatloaf
lines: Yield: 1 loaf using 1 pound beef | 3 servings | Prep: 15 minutes, plus prepared toppings | Bake: about 40–55 minutes | Rest: 10 minutes
Ingredients
1 pound ground beef
½ cup dry breadcrumbs
1 large egg
¼ cup milk
¼ cup grated Parmesan
½ cup shredded mozzarella
2 tablespoons ketchup
½ teaspoon Italian seasoning
Directions
Prepare: Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Line a rimmed baking sheet with parchment or foil, or lightly grease a small baking dish. Use a pan that leaves room around the loaf.
Mix breadcrumbs, milk, egg, Parmesan, and Italian seasoning; stand 5 minutes. Gently combine with beef. Reserve ketchup and mozzarella for topping.

Shape: Form gently into a compact loaf about 2–2½ inches thick. For the Master 1-pound beef batch, aim for roughly 7 by 4 inches. For serving-tab amounts, keep a similar thickness and adjust length, or make individual mini loaves.
Spread ketchup over the loaf before baking. Add mozzarella during the final 5–10 minutes, until melted.

Bake and Check: A loaf using 1 pound beef generally takes about 40–55 minutes at 350°F; topping and pan shape affect timing. Begin checking mini loaves after 20–25 minutes. Bake until a food thermometer in the center of the beef registers 160°F (71°C). Do not rely on color or the image’s full-batch time.
Rest and Slice: Carefully drain excess fat if needed. Rest for 10 minutes, then divide into the listed number of equal servings.

title: Loaded Mashed Potato Meatloaf
lines: Yield: 1 loaf using 1 pound beef | 3 servings | Prep: 15 minutes, plus prepared toppings | Bake: about 40–55 minutes | Rest: 10 minutes
Ingredients
1 pound ground beef
½ cup dry breadcrumbs
1 large egg
¼ cup milk
2 tablespoons ketchup
1 cup prepared mashed potatoes
½ cup shredded cheddar
3 slices cooked bacon, crumbled
Directions
Prepare: Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Line a rimmed baking sheet with parchment or foil, or lightly grease a small baking dish. Use a pan that leaves room around the loaf.
Mix breadcrumbs, milk, and egg; stand 5 minutes. Gently combine with beef. Reserve ketchup, mashed potatoes, cheese, and cooked bacon for topping.

Shape: Form gently into a compact loaf about 2–2½ inches thick. For the Master 1-pound beef batch, aim for roughly 7 by 4 inches. For serving-tab amounts, keep a similar thickness and adjust length, or make individual mini loaves.

Spread ketchup over the loaf and bake about 30 minutes. Add a layer of warm prepared mashed potatoes, then cheddar and cooked bacon. Continue baking until the beef reaches 160°F and the potato topping is hot through; allow about 10–20 minutes more.

Bake and Check: A loaf using 1 pound beef generally takes about 40–55 minutes at 350°F; topping and pan shape affect timing. Begin checking mini loaves after 20–25 minutes. Bake until a food thermometer in the center of the beef registers 160°F (71°C). Do not rely on color or the image’s full-batch time.
Rest and Slice: Carefully drain excess fat if needed. Rest for 10 minutes, then divide into the listed number of equal servings.
Notes
Mashed potatoes must be prepared before assembly. Warming them before topping helps the beef and potatoes finish together. This version may need longer than the other loaves.

title: Bacon Cheeseburger Meatloaf

Ingredients
1 pound ground beef
4 slices cooked bacon, crumbled
½ cup shredded cheddar
¼ cup dry breadcrumbs
1 large egg
2 tablespoons ketchup
1 tablespoon yellow mustard
2 tablespoons finely chopped pickles
Directions
Prepare: Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Line a rimmed baking sheet with parchment or foil, or lightly grease a small baking dish. Use a pan that leaves room around the loaf.
Mix breadcrumbs, egg, mustard, and chopped pickles. Stir in half the cooked bacon and half the cheddar. Gently combine with beef. Reserve ketchup and remaining bacon and cheddar for topping.

Shape: Form gently into a compact loaf about 2–2½ inches thick. For the Master 1-pound beef batch, aim for roughly 7 by 4 inches. For serving-tab amounts, keep a similar thickness and adjust length, or make individual mini loaves.
Spread ketchup over the loaf before baking. Add the reserved cheddar and cooked bacon for the final 5–10 minutes.

Bake and Check: A loaf using 1 pound beef generally takes about 40–55 minutes at 350°F; topping and pan shape affect timing. Begin checking mini loaves after 20–25 minutes. Bake until a food thermometer in the center of the beef registers 160°F (71°C). Do not rely on color or the image’s full-batch time.
Rest and Slice: Carefully drain excess fat if needed. Rest for 10 minutes, then divide into the listed number of equal servings.
Notes
There is no milk in the pictured formula. Use finely chopped, well-drained pickles and avoid overmixing for a tender loaf.

title: Homestyle Chicken Noodle Soup
lines: Yield: 6 servings | Serving size: one equal portion of the finished recipe | Prep: 10 minutes | Cook: 20–25 minutes
Ingredients
2 cups cooked shredded chicken
8 cups chicken broth
3 carrots, sliced
3 celery stalks, sliced
8 ounces dry egg noodles
Directions
Bring the broth, carrots, and celery to a boil in a pot. Reduce to a simmer and cook for 10 minutes, or until the vegetables are nearly tender.
Stir in the egg noodles and cooked chicken. Simmer for the noodle package’s recommended time, usually 6–10 minutes, until the noodles are tender and the chicken is hot throughout.
Taste before adding salt or pepper, if desired. Divide into equal portions and serve.
Notes
The noodles absorb broth as the soup stands. For leftovers, cook and store the noodles separately, or add a little broth when reheating.

title: Easy Saucy Sloppy Joes
lines: Yield: 3 servings | Serving size: 1 filled bun | Prep: 5 minutes | Cook: 15–20 minutes
Ingredients
1 pound ground beef
½ small onion, diced
15 ounces sloppy joe sauce (1 can)
3 hamburger buns
Directions
Brown the beef and onion in a large skillet over medium-high heat, breaking the beef into crumbles, for 8–10 minutes. Drain excess fat.
Stir in the sloppy joe sauce. Reduce the heat and simmer uncovered for 5–10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until hot and thick enough to spoon onto buns.
Divide the filling evenly among the buns and serve.
Notes

The image does not specify the sauce can size; the 1-pound master batch uses one 15-ounce can; use the listed sauce amount for your serving-size tab. Adjust the simmering time if your sauce is thinner or thicker.

title: Beef and Cheese Baked Ziti
lines: Yield: 8 servings | Serving size: one equal portion of the finished recipe | Prep: 15 minutes | Cook: 35–45 minutes
Ingredients
16 ounces dry ziti
1 pound ground beef
24 ounces marinara sauce
15 ounces ricotta cheese
2 cups shredded mozzarella cheese
Directions
Heat the oven to 375°F. Lightly grease a baking dish; use a 9-by-13-inch dish for the full batch or a smaller dish for a scaled recipe.
Boil the ziti in salted water until 1–2 minutes short of the package’s recommended time. Reserve a little pasta water, then drain.
Brown the beef in a skillet over medium-high heat, breaking it into crumbles. Drain excess fat and stir in the marinara.
Combine the pasta, meat sauce, ricotta, and half the mozzarella. Add a splash of reserved pasta water only if needed to loosen the mixture.

Transfer to the baking dish and top with the remaining mozzarella. Cover with foil and bake for 20 minutes; uncover and bake for 10–15 minutes more, until bubbling and hot throughout. A small scaled dish may finish sooner. Rest for 5 minutes, then divide into equal portions.
Notes
Use a smaller baking dish for reduced batches so the pasta stays moist; begin checking it early.

title: Loaded Bacon and Cheddar Potato Soup
lines: Yield: 6 servings | Serving size: one equal portion of the finished recipe | Prep: 15 minutes | Cook: 30–35 minutes
Ingredients
6 medium potatoes, diced (about 2½ pounds for the full batch)
8 slices bacon
4 cups chicken broth
2 cups milk
2 cups shredded cheddar cheese
Directions
Cook the bacon in a soup pot over medium heat until crisp. Transfer to a paper-towel-lined plate, then crumble. Drain the rendered fat from the pot.
Add the potatoes and broth. Bring to a boil, reduce to a simmer, and cook partially covered for 15–20 minutes, until the potatoes are very tender.
Mash some of the potatoes directly in the pot to thicken the soup. Stir in the milk and most of the bacon. Heat gently for 3–5 minutes without boiling.
Turn the heat to low and gradually stir in the cheddar until melted. Taste before adding salt or pepper, if desired. Divide into equal portions and garnish with the remaining bacon.
Notes
Use peeled potatoes for a smoother soup or scrub them well and leave the skins on. Add milk or broth a splash at a time if the soup becomes too thick.

title: BBQ Chicken and Coleslaw Sliders
lines: Yield: 6 servings (12 sliders) | Serving size: 2 sliders | Prep: 5 minutes | Cook: 5–8 minutes

title: Cheesy Tortilla Chip Taco Casserole
lines: Yield: 4 servings | Serving size: one equal portion of the finished recipe | Prep: 10 minutes | Cook: 25–30 minutes
Ingredients
1 pound ground beef
1 packet (1 ounce) taco seasoning
8 ounces salsa (about 1 cup)
5 ounces tortilla chips, lightly crushed
1 cup shredded cheddar cheese
Directions
Heat the oven to 375°F. Lightly grease a baking dish; use an 8-inch square dish for the 1-pound master batch, or a dish sized to your scaled recipe.
Brown the beef in a skillet over medium-high heat, breaking it into crumbles. Drain excess fat.
Add the taco seasoning and the amount of water directed on the seasoning packet, scaled to the amount used. Simmer according to the packet directions until the liquid has mostly reduced.
Layer half the chips, half the beef, half the salsa, and half the cheese in the dish. Repeat the layers.
Bake uncovered for 15–20 minutes, until the cheese melts and the casserole is hot throughout. Let stand for 5 minutes and divide into equal portions.
Notes
The image does not specify packet weights; this recipe assumes 1-ounce packets. Chips soften under the filling. Reserve a few chips to sprinkle on just before serving if you prefer extra crunch.

title: Creamy Cheeseburger Potato Soup
lines: Yield: 6 servings | Serving size: one equal portion of the finished recipe | Prep: 10 minutes | Cook: 25–35 minutes
Ingredients
1 pound ground beef
4 medium potatoes, diced (about 1½–2 pounds for the full batch)
4 cups chicken broth
2 cups milk
2 cups shredded cheddar cheese
Directions
Brown the beef in a soup pot over medium-high heat, breaking it into crumbles. Drain excess fat.
Add the potatoes and broth. Bring to a boil, reduce to a simmer, and cook partially covered for 15–20 minutes, until the potatoes are tender.
Mash a portion of the potatoes against the side of the pot to thicken the broth. Stir in the milk and heat gently for 3–5 minutes; do not boil.
Reduce the heat to low and gradually stir in the cheddar until melted and smooth. Taste before adding salt or pepper, if desired. Divide into equal portions and serve.
Notes
Freshly shredded cheddar melts more smoothly. For a thinner soup, add a splash of broth or milk.

title: Chicken Alfredo Lasagna
lines: Yield: 8 servings | Serving size: one equal portion | Prep: about 25–30 minutes | Bake: about 45–55 minutes | Rest: 10–15 minutes
Ingredients
12 lasagna noodles
2 cups cooked shredded chicken
4 cups prepared Alfredo sauce
15 ounces ricotta cheese
2 cups shredded mozzarella cheese
½ cup grated Parmesan cheese
2 cups fresh spinach, chopped
1 teaspoon garlic powder
Directions
Heat the oven to 375°F. Lightly grease a 9-by-13-inch baking dish for the full 8-serving batch; use a smaller dish for a scaled batch.

Cook regular lasagna noodles until just flexible and slightly firmer than al dente, following the package directions. Drain and lay flat. Cut cooked noodles to fit smaller dishes as needed; do not substitute dry oven-ready noodles without adjusting the method.

Wilt the spinach in a covered skillet with the water clinging to its washed leaves. Cool slightly and squeeze out excess liquid. Mix the spinach with the ricotta, garlic powder, and half the Parmesan.
Set aside one quarter of the Alfredo sauce. Combine the remaining sauce with the cooked chicken. Spread a thin coating of reserved sauce over the dish.

Make three layers, each using one third of the noodles, ricotta mixture, and chicken mixture. Divide half the mozzarella between the first two layers. Cover the last layer with the rest of the reserved sauce, remaining mozzarella, and remaining Parmesan.

Cover with lightly greased foil. Bake for 35–40 minutes, then uncover and bake for 10–15 minutes, until bubbling throughout and the center reaches 165°F. Smaller dishes may finish sooner; check early.
Rest for 10–15 minutes before cutting into equal portions.
Notes

Use your cookbook's Alfredo sauce or a prepared sauce. Four cups are needed for the master batch; the separate two-serving Alfredo sauce recipe makes about 1¼ cups, so measure the finished sauce rather than assuming two servings equals this amount.
Source

Ingredients from Corey's supplied lasagna image. Directions adapted for these quantities using a similar layering method from Epicure: https://epicure.com/en-us/pages/recipes/alfredo-chicken-lasagna . This is not a verified original recipe from the image's publisher.
