1 ¼ cups shredded mozzarella cheese
5/16 cup grated Parmesan cheese
1 ¼ cups fresh spinach, chopped
⅝ teaspoon garlic powder
Directions
Heat the oven to 375°F. Lightly grease a 9-by-13-inch baking dish for the full 8-serving batch; use a smaller dish for a scaled batch.

Cook regular lasagna noodles until just flexible and slightly firmer than al dente, following the package directions. Drain and lay flat. Cut cooked noodles to fit smaller dishes as needed; do not substitute dry oven-ready noodles without adjusting the method.

Wilt the spinach in a covered skillet with the water clinging to its washed leaves. Cool slightly and squeeze out excess liquid. Mix the spinach with the ricotta, garlic powder, and half the Parmesan.
Set aside one quarter of the Alfredo sauce. Combine the remaining sauce with the cooked chicken. Spread a thin coating of reserved sauce over the dish.

Make three layers, each using one third of the noodles, ricotta mixture, and chicken mixture. Divide half the mozzarella between the first two layers. Cover the last layer with the rest of the reserved sauce, remaining mozzarella, and remaining Parmesan.

Cover with lightly greased foil. Bake for 35–40 minutes, then uncover and bake for 10–15 minutes, until bubbling throughout and the center reaches 165°F. Smaller dishes may finish sooner; check early.
Rest for 10–15 minutes before cutting into equal portions.
Notes

Use your cookbook's Alfredo sauce or a prepared sauce. Four cups are needed for the master batch; the separate two-serving Alfredo sauce recipe makes about 1¼ cups, so measure the finished sauce rather than assuming two servings equals this amount.

title: Louisiana Red Beans and Rice
lines: Yield: 6 bowls | Serving size: about 1 cup bean mixture over 1 cup white rice
Ingredients
2 cups dry red kidney beans
12 to 16 ounces smoked sausage, sliced
1 onion, diced
1 green bell pepper, diced
3 celery ribs, diced
4 garlic cloves, minced
1 teaspoon smoked paprika
1 teaspoon dried thyme
1 teaspoon Cajun seasoning
2 bay leaves
3 cups chicken broth
Salt, black pepper, and hot sauce, to taste
6 cups cooked white rice, for serving
Directions
Sort and rinse the kidney beans. Soak overnight in the refrigerator, then drain and rinse.
Cover with fresh water and boil at a full rolling boil for 30 minutes. Reduce the heat and simmer until completely tender, 60 to 90 minutes. Drain, reserving 1 to 2 cups cooking liquid.
Brown the sausage in a large pot. Add the onion, bell pepper, and celery and cook until softened.
Add the garlic, smoked paprika, thyme, Cajun seasoning, and bay leaves; cook for 1 minute.
Add the cooked beans and chicken broth. Simmer for 30 to 45 minutes, adding reserved bean liquid if needed.
Mash some beans against the side of the pot to thicken. Season with salt, black pepper, and hot sauce, then remove the bay leaves.
Divide into 6 portions and serve each over 1 cup cooked white rice.
Notes
Never place raw or merely soaked kidney beans directly into a slow cooker.

title: Copycat Fritos Bean Dip
lines: Yield: about 1 1/2 cups, 6 servings | Serving size: 1/4 cup
Ingredients
One 15-ounce can pinto beans, drained but not rinsed
4 slices pickled jalapeno
1 tablespoon juice from the jalapeno jar, plus more if needed
1/2 teaspoon salt
1/2 teaspoon granulated sugar
1/4 teaspoon onion powder
1/4 teaspoon paprika
1/8 teaspoon garlic powder
1/8 teaspoon cayenne pepper
Directions
Place the drained pinto beans, jalapeno slices, jalapeno juice, salt, sugar, onion powder, paprika, garlic powder, and cayenne pepper in a food processor or blender.
Blend on high until completely smooth, stopping to scrape down the sides as needed.
If the dip is too thick, blend in additional jalapeno juice 1 teaspoon at a time until it reaches the desired consistency.
Transfer the dip to a covered container and refrigerate for at least 1 hour so the flavor and texture can develop.
Stir before serving. Serve chilled or at room temperature with Fritos corn chips.
Notes
Makes about 1 1/2 cups. Canned beans vary in saltiness; begin with 1/4 teaspoon salt, taste, and add more if needed.

title: Smooth and Creamy Classic Hummus
lines: Yield: about 2 cups, 8 servings | Serving size: 1/4 cup
Ingredients
1/3 cup good-quality tahini
2 to 4 tablespoons cold water, divided, plus more if needed
2 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil
1/2 teaspoon ground cumin
3/4 teaspoon fine sea salt, plus more to taste
2 medium garlic cloves, peeled and smashed
2 to 3 tablespoons fresh lemon juice (about 1 lemon)
1 (15-ounce) can chickpeas, rinsed and well drained (about 1 1/2 cups / drained; brand-dependent)
Optional toppings: extra-virgin olive oil, chopped fresh parsley, ground sumac or paprika, and toasted pine nuts
Directions
Blend the Base: Add the tahini, 2 tablespoons of the cold water, olive oil, cumin, salt, garlic, and lemon juice to a food processor. Process until completely smooth.

title: Crispy Salmon or Tuna Patties
lines: Yield: 6 patties | Serving size: 1 patty
Ingredients
Two 5-ounce cans salmon or tuna, drained
1 large egg
1/2 cup breadcrumbs or finely crushed crackers
1/4 cup mayonnaise
1 tablespoon mustard
1/2 teaspoon garlic powder
1/2 teaspoon onion powder
Salt and black pepper to taste
2 tablespoons oil, for frying
Optional: chopped parsley, green onion, or a squeeze of lemon
Directions
Combine the drained salmon or tuna, egg, breadcrumbs, mayonnaise, mustard, garlic powder, onion powder, salt, black pepper, and optional herbs.
Shape the mixture into six small patties. If the mixture feels soft, chill it for 10 to 15 minutes.
Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat.
Cook the patties for 3 to 4 minutes per side, until crisp, golden, and heated through.
Serve with lemon, tartar sauce, or a simple salad.

title: Creamy Dill Pickle Albacore Tuna Salad
lines: Yield: about 2 cups, 4 servings | Serving size: 1/2 cup filling
Ingredients
2 (5-ounce) cans wild albacore tuna packed in water, drained very well
1/3 cup high-quality mayonnaise, such as Duke's or Kewpie
1 tablespoon Dijon mustard
1 tablespoon dill pickle juice
1 tablespoon fresh lemon juice
1/4 cup finely diced red onion
1/4 cup finely diced dill pickles
1 celery stalk, finely diced
1 tablespoon finely chopped fresh dill, or 1 teaspoon dried dill weed
1/4 teaspoon garlic powder
1/4 teaspoon onion powder
Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
Sliced bread, sourdough, lettuce wraps, or crackers, for serving
Directions
Drain and Flake: Place the drained tuna in a medium bowl and break it apart with a fork until it reaches your preferred texture.
Mix the Base: In a small bowl, stir together the mayonnaise, Dijon mustard, pickle juice, lemon juice, garlic powder, onion powder, and dill until smooth.
Add the Crunch: Fold the dressing, red onion, dill pickles, and celery into the tuna until evenly combined.
Season: Taste and add salt and freshly ground black pepper as needed.
Chill and Serve: Cover and refrigerate for 20 to 30 minutes so the flavors can blend, then serve on toasted bread, sourdough, in lettuce wraps, or with crackers.
Notes
Makes enough filling for about 4 sandwiches.
For the best texture and flavor, use good-quality wild-caught albacore packed in water, such as Wild Planet, and drain it thoroughly.
The Dijon, pickle juice, and lemon make this version bright and tangy. After chilling, add 1 to 2 tablespoons more mayonnaise if you prefer it creamier.
If using dried dill weed, the chilling time helps it soften and release its flavor.

title: Thick and Hearty Chicken and Rice Soup
lines: Yield: 2 generous bowls | Serving size: 1/2 recipe, about 2 cups
Ingredients
1 large boneless, skinless chicken breast, cut into bite-size pieces
1/3 cup dry jasmine rice, rinsed thoroughly
2 tablespoons butter
2 tablespoons all-purpose flour
1/2 yellow onion, finely chopped
1 large carrot, diced
1 celery stalk, diced
2 garlic cloves, minced
3 cups chicken broth, plus up to 1 additional cup as needed
2 tablespoons finely chopped fresh dill
1/2 teaspoon poultry seasoning
1/2 teaspoon onion powder
1/2 teaspoon garlic powder
1/2 teaspoon salt, plus more to taste
1/4 teaspoon black pepper
1 bay leaf
Directions
Melt the butter in a large soup pot over medium heat. Add the onion, carrot, and celery and cook for 5 to 6 minutes, until softened. Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Sprinkle the flour over the vegetables. Stir constantly for 1 to 2 minutes, until the flour forms a thick coating and the raw flour smell fades.

Slowly pour in the chicken broth in small splashes, stirring constantly. Add the chicken, bay leaf, poultry seasoning, onion powder, garlic powder, salt, and black pepper. Bring to a gentle boil, then reduce the heat, cover, and simmer for 10 minutes.

Stir in the rinsed jasmine rice. Cover and simmer for 12 to 15 minutes, stirring every few minutes and scraping the bottom, until the rice is tender and the chicken is cooked through. Add more broth if the soup becomes thicker than you like.
Remove from the heat and discard the bay leaf. Stir in the fresh dill and rest for 2 minutes. Taste and adjust the salt and black pepper before serving.
Notes
The soup will continue to thicken as it rests.
For leftovers, the rice will absorb more broth overnight. Add a splash of broth before reheating and warm gently.

3/4 teaspoon poultry seasoning
3/4 teaspoon onion powder
3/4 teaspoon garlic powder
3/4 teaspoon salt, plus more to taste
3/8 teaspoon black pepper
1 to 2 bay leaves
Directions
Melt the butter in a large soup pot over medium heat. Add the onion, carrot, and celery and cook for 5 to 6 minutes, until softened. Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Sprinkle the flour over the vegetables. Stir constantly for 1 to 2 minutes, until the flour forms a thick coating and the raw flour smell fades.

Slowly pour in the chicken broth in small splashes, stirring constantly. Add the chicken, bay leaf, poultry seasoning, onion powder, garlic powder, salt, and black pepper. Bring to a gentle boil, then reduce the heat, cover, and simmer for 10 minutes.

Stir in the rinsed jasmine rice. Cover and simmer for 12 to 15 minutes, stirring every few minutes and scraping the bottom, until the rice is tender and the chicken is cooked through. Add more broth if the soup becomes thicker than you like.
Remove from the heat and discard the bay leaf. Stir in the fresh dill and rest for 2 minutes. Taste and adjust the salt and black pepper before serving.
Notes
The soup will continue to thicken as it rests.
For leftovers, the rice will absorb more broth overnight. Add a splash of broth before reheating and warm gently.

title: Zuppa Toscana (Creamy Sausage, Potato and Kale Soup)
lines: Yield: about 12 cups, 8 servings | Serving size: 1 1/2 cups
Ingredients
1 pound ground Italian sausage, spicy or mild
3 garlic cloves, minced
1 medium white onion, diced
1 1/2 pounds Yukon Gold potatoes, cut into 1/2-inch dice
5 to 6 cups low-sodium chicken stock
2 to 3 cups chopped fresh kale, tough stems removed
1 cup heavy whipping cream
Fine sea salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
6 slices bacon, cooked and crumbled
Directions

Cook the sausage in a large stockpot over medium-high heat, breaking it into small pieces, until browned and cooked through. Transfer it to a plate with a slotted spoon. Reserve 1 tablespoon of drippings in the pot and discard the rest.
Add the onion and cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally. Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute.

Return the sausage to the pot. Add the potatoes and 5 cups of stock. Bring to a simmer, reduce the heat to medium-low, and cook for 10 to 15 minutes, until the potatoes are tender. Add more stock if a thinner soup is desired.
Stir in the kale and cream. Maintain a gentle simmer for 5 minutes, until the kale is tender and the soup is heated through.
Taste and season with salt and black pepper.
Ladle into 8 equal servings and garnish each bowl with crumbled bacon.
Notes
Use 2 cups of kale for a milder flavor or 3 cups for a greener, heartier soup.
Drain the cooked sausage thoroughly to reduce excess grease.
The soup thickens as it stands; add a splash of stock when reheating if needed.
Source
Adapted from Gimme Some Oven's Zuppa Toscana (Olive Garden Copycat).

title: Corey’s Hearty Chili
lines: Yield: about 3–4 servings | Prep: 10 minutes | Cook: about 1 hour 20 minutes
Ingredients
1 pound ground beef
1½ garlic cloves, minced, or 2 small cloves
4 ounces tomato sauce, about ½ cup
1½ ounces tomato paste, about 2 tablespoons plus 1 teaspoon
1 tablespoon chili powder, plus more to taste
½ teaspoon ground cumin
½ teaspoon ground oregano
½ teaspoon kosher salt, plus more to taste (weight varies by brand)
⅛ teaspoon cayenne pepper, plus more to taste
1 can (15 ounces) kidney or pinto beans, or a mixture, drained and rinsed
2 tablespoons masa harina or regular cornmeal
2 tablespoons water, for mixing with the masa harina
Up to 6 tablespoons additional water, as needed during simmering
Shredded cheddar, crumbled cooked bacon, and sliced jalapeños, for topping
Directions
Brown the Beef: In a heavy pot over medium heat, cook the ground beef and garlic, breaking the meat into crumbles, until fully cooked. Drain most of the excess fat.

Season and Simmer: Stir in the tomato sauce, tomato paste, chili powder, cumin, oregano, salt, and cayenne. Cover and simmer over low heat for 1 hour, stirring occasionally. Add the additional water a tablespoon or two at a time as needed to prevent sticking.
Add the Beans and Thickener: Stir in the drained beans. In a small bowl, mix the masa harina with the measured mixing water until smooth, then stir it into the chili.

Finish: Simmer gently for another 10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until thickened and the beans are heated through. If using regular cornmeal, allow extra simmering time until it softens. Add a splash of water if the chili becomes too thick.
Serve: Taste and adjust the seasonings. Spoon into bowls and top with shredded cheddar, crumbled cooked bacon, and sliced jalapeños as desired.
Notes
Masa harina gives a smoother texture and a distinct corn flavor. Regular cornmeal may leave a slightly grainier finish.
The full 1-pound batch makes about 3 to 4 servings. The serving tabs use 4 portions per batch; divide the finished chili evenly.
Bean and topping weights vary by brand. Bean weights listed below are before draining; drain and rinse before use.

title: Corey’s Incredible Creamy Clam Chowder
lines: Yield: about 9 cups | 6 servings of about 1½ cups | Prep: 15 minutes | Cook: about 1 hour
Ingredients
6 strips thick-cut bacon, or salt pork; reserve 2 tablespoons drippings
2 tablespoons butter
1 medium yellow onion, diced
2 ribs celery, diced
3 garlic cloves, minced
1 teaspoon hot sauce, or ½ teaspoon Tabasco sauce
1 teaspoon Worcestershire sauce
⅓ cup all-purpose flour
1 cup chicken broth
3 cups half-and-half
8 fluid ounces bottled clam juice (1 cup)
1 chicken bouillon cube (brand-dependent weight)
1 bay leaf
1¼ pounds potatoes, peeled and diced
3 cans (6.5 ounces each / before draining) chopped clams, juices reserved
½ teaspoon dried oregano
½ teaspoon dried parsley
¼ teaspoon dried thyme
¼ teaspoon salt, then adjust to taste
⅛ teaspoon smoked paprika
⅛ teaspoon ground black pepper
Fresh parsley and freshly cracked black pepper, for serving
Directions

Cook the Bacon: Cook the bacon slowly over low heat in a heavy soup pot until crisp. Transfer to a paper towel-lined plate, then chop when cool. Reserve the listed amount of bacon drippings. Wipe away any burned spots, keeping the browned bits for flavor.

Soften the Vegetables: Add the reserved drippings and butter to the pot over medium heat. Stir and scrape up the browned bits. Add the onion and celery and cook for 5 to 6 minutes until softened. Stir in the garlic, hot sauce, Worcestershire, oregano, dried parsley, thyme, salt, smoked paprika, and ground pepper. Cook for 1 minute.
Make the Roux: Sprinkle in the flour and cook for 2 minutes, stirring continuously.

Build the Broth: Slowly stir in the chicken broth in small additions, scraping the pot as you go. Gradually add the half-and-half in the same way. Stir in the bouillon, bay leaf, reserved liquid from the canned clams, and bottled clam juice. Keep the clams aside.
Reduce Gently: Bring just to a gentle bubble, then reduce to a low simmer. Cook partially covered for 20 minutes, stirring occasionally. Avoid a hard boil.

Cook the Potatoes: Add the peeled, diced potatoes. Simmer gently for 20 to 25 minutes, stirring occasionally, until fork-tender. Check smaller batches early and add a splash of broth if the chowder becomes too thick.
Finish with Clams: Reduce the heat to low. Stir in the clams and heat gently for about 5 minutes. Remove and discard the bay leaf. Taste and adjust the seasoning.
Serve: Ladle into bowls and garnish with the chopped bacon, fresh parsley, and freshly cracked pepper. Serve with crusty bread if desired.
Notes
Clams: Reserve all juice from the canned clams. Bar Harbor chopped clams and bottled clam juice are the original recipe’s suggested brands.

Fresh-Clam Option: For the full batch, substitute 1 heaping cup chopped, already steamed fresh clams and 1½ cups total clam juice for the canned clams and bottled clam juice. Clean and steam the fresh clams before chopping. Scale both amounts proportionally for smaller batches.
Potatoes: Yukon Gold potatoes give a creamy texture. Red potatoes hold their shape well. Russets also work, but may break apart more easily.
Consistency: Simmer the broth before adding the potatoes so it can reduce without overcooking them. Thin with a splash of broth or half-and-half if needed.

Flavor Options: Frank’s hot sauce is the original suggestion. Hot sauce and Worcestershire add background flavor; heat varies by brand. Soy sauce may replace Worcestershire. Salt pork may replace bacon.
Season to Taste: Bacon, clam juice, canned clam liquid, and bouillon vary in saltiness. Taste before adding extra salt.
Serving Sizes: The original yield is about 9 cups. This book treats that as 6 servings of about 1½ cups each. Final volume varies with evaporation.

Small Batches: Use a smaller pot, keep the simmer gentle, and check the potatoes early. For fractional bouillon cubes, crush and measure or weigh the needed portion. Buy clams by the listed can-equivalent weight, reserve their liquid, and portion evenly.

title: Karissa Stevens’ New England Clam Chowder
lines: Estimated yield: 8 servings | Divide finished chowder into 8 equal portions
Ingredients
8 tablespoons butter (1 stick)
8 ounces bacon, chopped
2 cups chopped celery
1 large onion, chopped
24 ounces chopped clams in juice, juice retained
2 cups additional clam juice
2 cups chicken or vegetable broth
32 ounces potatoes, peeled, diced, and pre-boiled
2 cups heavy cream
½ teaspoon black pepper
Celery salt, to taste
6 tablespoons cornstarch
12 tablespoons cold water, for the slurry
4 tablespoons chopped fresh dill
Salt, to taste, optional; add only after tasting
Directions
Prepare the Potatoes: Peel and dice the potatoes. Boil in water until just fork-tender, then drain and set aside.
Cook the Bacon: In a large heavy soup pot over medium heat, cook the chopped bacon until fully cooked. Transfer to a plate. Leave the drippings in the pot.
Soften the Vegetables: Add the butter to the pot and melt over medium heat. Add the celery and onion and cook, stirring occasionally, until softened.
Simmer the Base: Add the cooked bacon, chopped clams with their juice, additional clam juice, and chicken or vegetable broth. Bring to a gentle simmer and cook for about 10 minutes.
Add Potatoes and Cream: Gently stir in the cooked potatoes, then slowly add the heavy cream. Warm gently, stirring; avoid a vigorous boil.

Thicken: Whisk the cornstarch and cold water until smooth. Stir the slurry again just before pouring it gradually into the chowder. Bring to a gentle simmer and stir for a few minutes until thickened. Stop adding slurry when the consistency suits you.
Season and Finish: Add the black pepper and celery salt to taste. Fold in the fresh dill and warm through. Taste before adding optional salt, then serve.
Notes

Yield was not supplied with the recipe. For scaling, this book uses an estimated 8 servings for the full batch. Divide the finished batch evenly; smaller serving-tab batches are proportional portions of that estimate.
This entry follows the recipe supplied by Corey and attributed to Karissa Stevens. The quantities have not been independently verified against her subscription recipe.
Bacon is cooked separately before the clams are added. This clarifies the supplied method while retaining the ingredients.
The clam quantity is listed as clams in juice; the source does not specify drained meat weight. Retain the accompanying juice. Product packing and salt levels vary by brand.
The full cornstarch slurry makes a thick chowder. Add gradually and use only as much as desired. Bacon, broth, clam juice, and celery salt can already supply plenty of salt.

title: Chef John's Shrimp Étouffée
lines: Yield: 4 generous servings | Serving size: one equal share of shrimp and sauce, with ½ cup cooked rice | Total: about 1 hour 15 minutes
Spice Blend
¾ teaspoon paprika
¼ teaspoon ground thyme
¼ teaspoon dried oregano
¼ teaspoon cayenne pepper
¼ teaspoon garlic powder
¼ teaspoon onion powder
¼ teaspoon white pepper
¼ teaspoon black pepper
Ingredients
2 pounds raw shrimp, peeled and deveined
½ teaspoon salt, plus more to taste
1 tablespoon vegetable oil
1 ¾ cups chicken stock, plus extra if needed
3 tablespoons butter
⅓ cup diced onion
⅓ cup diced green bell pepper
⅓ cup thinly sliced celery
2 tablespoons all-purpose flour
½ cup diced tomatoes
½ teaspoon Worcestershire sauce
Hot sauce, to taste
2 cups cooked white rice
¼ cup sliced green onions
Extra cayenne, optional garnish
Directions
Combine the spice blend. Drain thawed shrimp for 15 minutes and pat dry. Toss with the measured salt and 1 teaspoon of the blend.
Sear shrimp in hot oil for about 2 minutes, turning once. Remove to a bowl; reserve the liquid they release.
Combine those juices with stock to make 2 cups total liquid.
In the same pan, lightly brown the butter. Soften onion, pepper, and celery for 5 minutes; add remaining spice blend.
Stir in flour for 3–4 minutes, then tomatoes for 3 minutes. Gradually whisk in stock mixture; simmer 3–5 minutes to thicken.
Add Worcestershire, hot sauce, and salt to taste. Return shrimp; simmer until opaque throughout, about 1 minute. Serve with rice, green onions, and optional cayenne.
Notes
Use raw shrimp; avoid overcooking when returning them to the sauce. Scaled cooking times are approximate. Ground thyme follows the Allrecipes version.
Source

title: Creamy Sauerkraut and Dill Potato Salad
lines: Yield: 6 servings | Serving size: 3/4 cup
Ingredients
2 pounds russet potatoes, about 4 medium, unpeeled and thoroughly scrubbed
1 tablespoon coarse salt, for the cooking water
1 cup sauerkraut, thoroughly drained and firmly squeezed dry
1/4 cup fresh dill, finely chopped
6 green onions, white and light green parts, thinly sliced
Optional: 1/2 cup yellow onion, finely minced, for a stronger onion flavor
3/4 cup mayonnaise
1 tablespoon yellow or Dijon mustard
1/2 teaspoon garlic powder
1/2 teaspoon onion powder
Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
Directions
Cut the scrubbed, unpeeled potatoes into uniform 1/2-to-3/4-inch cubes.
Place the potatoes in a large pot and cover with cold water by about 2 inches. Add salt, bring to a boil, then reduce to a gentle boil and cook for 10 to 12 minutes, until just fork-tender.
Drain thoroughly, spread the potatoes on a baking sheet or large plate, and cool completely.
Whisk the mayonnaise, mustard, garlic powder, onion powder, and black pepper together until smooth.
Add the cooled potatoes, sauerkraut, green onions, optional yellow onion, and dill. Fold gently so the potato cubes keep their shape.
Taste and adjust the salt or black pepper. Cover and refrigerate for at least 1 hour before serving.
Notes
Always cool the potatoes completely before adding the mayonnaise so the dressing stays thick and creamy.

title: Skin-On Garlic Dill Pickle Potato Salad
lines: Yield: 8 servings | Serving size: 3/4 cup
Ingredients
6 small-to-medium russet potatoes, about 2 1/2 pounds, scrubbed, unpeeled, and cut into bite-size chunks
Salt, for the cooking water
1 to 2 celery ribs, finely diced
1/2 yellow onion, finely minced
2 to 3 dill pickles, finely diced
1 to 2 tablespoons dill pickle brine, divided
2 tablespoons fresh dill, finely chopped
1/2 cup mayonnaise
1 to 2 tablespoons yellow or Dijon mustard
1 small garlic clove, finely grated or minced
1 teaspoon fresh lemon or lime juice, divided
Salt and black pepper, to taste
Optional: 1/4 teaspoon garlic powder or paprika
Directions
Place the potatoes in a large pot and cover with cold water by 1 inch. Salt generously, bring to a boil, then reduce to a simmer. Cook for 10 to 12 minutes, until just fork-tender, and drain well.
Transfer the warm potatoes to a bowl. Gently toss with half the pickle brine and half the lemon or lime juice, then cool completely.
For a milder onion flavor, soak the minced onion in cold water or a little pickle brine for 5 minutes. Drain and pat dry.
Whisk together the mayonnaise, mustard, garlic, remaining citrus juice, black pepper, and optional garlic powder or paprika.
Gently fold the cooled potatoes, pickles, celery, onion, and dill into the dressing. Taste and add more mustard, pickle brine, salt, or pepper as desired.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 1 hour before serving.
Notes
Let the potatoes cool completely before adding the mayonnaise so the dressing stays thick and creamy.
Russet potatoes are starchy, so fold gently to help the chunks hold their shape.

Salt, for the cooking water
4 to 6 celery ribs, finely diced
1 1/2 yellow onions, finely minced
6 to 9 dill pickles, finely diced

3 small garlic cloves, finely grated or minced

Directions

Divide the potatoes between two large pots, or use one very large stockpot. Cover with cold water by 1 inch and salt generously. Bring to a boil, reduce to a simmer, and cook for 10 to 12 minutes, until just fork-tender. Drain well.
Transfer the warm potatoes to a very large bowl or divide them between two bowls. Gently toss with 1/4 cup pickle brine and 1 1/2 teaspoons lemon or lime juice, then cool completely.

Notes

For the best flavor, prepare it up to 1 day ahead and fold gently before serving.

title: Annette Freckles' Foolproof Mexican Rice
lines: Yield: about 3 cups, 9 side servings | Serving size: 1/3 cup
Ingredients
1 cup dry long-grain white or jasmine rice, unwashed
1 tablespoon neutral oil, such as avocado or canola oil
3 cups water
5 tablespoons plain tomato sauce
1 tablespoon Knorr chicken bouillon or tomato bouillon
Directions
Heat a medium saucepan with a tight-fitting lid over medium-high heat.
Add the oil and dry, unwashed rice. Toast for 3 to 4 minutes, stirring often, until the rice is lightly golden and smells nutty.
Carefully pour in the water; it may steam. Stir in the tomato sauce and bouillon until the bouillon dissolves.
Cover tightly and cook over medium-high heat for 10 minutes without lifting the lid.
Turn off the heat and leave the covered pan on the hot burner for 5 minutes without peeking.
Move the pan completely off the burner and let it rest, still covered, for 10 minutes.
Uncover, fluff gently with a fork, and divide into 9 equal portions of about 1/3 cup each.
Notes
This method intentionally uses unwashed rice and a strict 1 cup rice to 3 cups water ratio.
Exact timing can vary with the pan and stove. On gas or induction, which cools quickly, keep the pan covered and undisturbed during both resting periods.
Bouillon can be salty, so taste before adding any extra salt.
Source
Adapted from Annette Freckles' Easy Mexican Rice video.

title: Classic Potato Salad
lines: Yield: about 8 side servings | Serving size: ⅛ of the finished salad
Ingredients
3 pounds potatoes
6 large eggs
1 cup mayonnaise
2 tablespoons Dijon mustard
2 tablespoons white vinegar or dill pickle juice
1 celery stalk, diced
1 small red onion, finely chopped
2 green onions, chopped
1 teaspoon salt
½ teaspoon black pepper
½ teaspoon paprika, optional
Directions

Scrub the potatoes and cut into even ¾-inch pieces, leaving the skins on if desired. Place in a pot, cover with cold water by 1 inch, and bring to a boil. Reduce to a gentle simmer and cook for 10–15 minutes, until just fork-tender. Drain well.

While the potatoes cook, place the eggs in a saucepan and cover with cold water by 1 inch. Bring to a boil, cover, remove from the heat, and let stand for 12 minutes. Transfer to ice water, cool, peel, and chop.
Spread the potatoes in a shallow layer to cool until no longer warm. For faster cooling, place the shallow tray in the refrigerator.

Whisk the mayonnaise, Dijon, vinegar or pickle juice, salt, and pepper in a large bowl. Gently fold in the potatoes, chopped eggs, celery, red onion, and green onions. Sprinkle with the paprika if using.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 1 hour. Taste and adjust the seasoning before serving; divide into equal side-dish portions.
Notes
For a scaled recipe calling for part of an egg, hard-boil a whole egg, chop it, and use the listed fraction; save the rest for another meal.
Source: Ingredient list from Corey's supplied potato salad image. Directions and estimated yields developed for this cookbook.

title: Loaded Baked Potato Salad
lines: Yield: about 8 side servings | Serving size: ⅛ of the finished salad
Ingredients
3 pounds potatoes
2 cups shredded sharp cheddar cheese
8 ounces bacon, cooked and crumbled
1 cup sour cream
½ cup mayonnaise
2 green onions, chopped
½ teaspoon garlic powder
1 teaspoon salt
½ teaspoon black pepper
Directions

Heat the oven to 400°F. Scrub the potatoes, prick them with a fork, and bake on a tray for 45–60 minutes, until tender. Timing depends on potato size. Let cool, then cut into bite-sized chunks; keep the skins on if desired.

If starting with raw bacon, cook it in a skillet until crisp, drain on paper towels, then crumble. The listed bacon amount is the image’s approximate amount to prepare; bacon weight varies after cooking.

Cover and refrigerate for at least 1 hour. Garnish with the reserved bacon and green onions, then divide into equal side-dish portions.

title: Warm German Potato Salad
lines: Yield: about 8 side servings | Serving size: ⅛ of the finished salad
Ingredients
3 pounds waxy potatoes, such as red or Yukon Gold
6 ounces bacon, diced
1 small red onion, finely chopped
⅓ cup apple cider vinegar
¼ cup chicken or vegetable broth
2 tablespoons Dijon mustard
2 tablespoons chopped fresh parsley
1 tablespoon chopped fresh dill
½ teaspoon salt
½ teaspoon black pepper
Directions

Scrub the potatoes and cut into even ¾-inch pieces, leaving the skins on if desired. Place in a pot, cover with cold water by 1 inch, and bring to a boil. Reduce to a gentle simmer and cook for 10–15 minutes, until just fork-tender. Drain well.
While the potatoes cook, fry the diced bacon in a large skillet over medium heat until crisp. Transfer the bacon to a plate, leaving a thin coating of drippings in the skillet; drain excess fat.
Add the onion and cook over medium heat for 4–5 minutes, until softened. Stir in the vinegar, broth, Dijon, salt, and pepper. Simmer gently for 1–2 minutes.
Add the warm drained potatoes and gently toss with the dressing. Fold in the bacon, parsley, and dill. Let stand for 5 minutes, then divide into equal side-dish portions and serve warm.
Notes
This is a tangy, savory version without added sugar. If making ahead, refrigerate promptly and reheat gently with a splash of broth.
Source: Ingredient list from Corey's supplied potato salad image. Directions and estimated yields developed for this cookbook.

title: Greek Potato Salad with Feta
lines: Yield: about 8 side servings | Serving size: ⅛ of the finished salad
Ingredients
3 pounds potatoes
½ cup olive oil
¼ cup lemon juice
1 teaspoon dried oregano
½ teaspoon salt
½ teaspoon black pepper
½ red onion, thinly sliced
1 cup chopped cucumber
1 cup cherry tomatoes, halved
1 cup crumbled feta cheese
2 tablespoons chopped fresh parsley
Directions

Scrub the potatoes and cut into even ¾-inch pieces, leaving the skins on if desired. Place in a pot, cover with cold water by 1 inch, and bring to a boil. Reduce to a gentle simmer and cook for 10–15 minutes, until just fork-tender. Drain well.
Whisk the olive oil, lemon juice, oregano, salt, and pepper. Gently toss half the dressing with the warm drained potatoes, then let cool.
Fold in the red onion, cucumber, tomatoes, feta, parsley, and remaining dressing.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 1 hour. Toss gently and taste before adding more salt, since feta is salty. Divide into equal side-dish portions.
Notes
The image shows olives in the finished salad but does not list them in the ingredients; this recipe follows the ingredient list. Add sliced olives only if desired.

title: Creamy Dill Pickle Potato Salad
lines: Yield: about 8 side servings | Serving size: ⅛ of the finished salad
Ingredients
3 pounds potatoes
1 cup mayonnaise
½ cup sour cream
1 cup chopped dill pickles
½ small red onion, finely chopped
2 tablespoons chopped fresh dill
1 tablespoon dill pickle juice
1 teaspoon garlic powder
½ teaspoon salt
½ teaspoon black pepper
Directions

Scrub the potatoes and cut into even ¾-inch pieces, leaving the skins on if desired. Place in a pot, cover with cold water by 1 inch, and bring to a boil. Reduce to a gentle simmer and cook for 10–15 minutes, until just fork-tender. Drain well.
Spread the potatoes in a shallow layer to cool until no longer warm. For faster cooling, place the shallow tray in the refrigerator.
Whisk the mayonnaise, sour cream, pickle juice, garlic powder, salt, and pepper. Gently fold in the cooled potatoes, chopped pickles, red onion, and dill.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 1 hour. Taste and adjust the seasoning before serving; divide into equal side-dish portions.
Notes
Taste before adding extra salt; the pickles and brine already contribute salt. This is a separate version from Corey's existing Skin-On Garlic Dill Pickle Potato Salad.
Source: Ingredient list from Corey's supplied potato salad image. Directions and estimated yields developed for this cookbook.

title: Homemade Instant-Style Coffee Powder
lines: Yield: varies, about 24 drinks | Serving size: 1 teaspoon powder in 8 ounces water
Ingredients
1 cup freshly ground coffee beans, medium grind
4 cups hot water, just off the boil
Equipment
Fine-mesh strainer
Coffee filter or cheesecloth, recommended for removing fine sediment
Medium saucepan
Rimmed baking sheet
Parchment paper
Spice grinder or mortar and pestle, optional
Directions
Steep the Coffee: Place the coffee grounds in a heat-safe container and pour the hot water over them. Stir and steep for 10 minutes.
Strain: Pour the coffee through a fine-mesh strainer lined with a coffee filter or cheesecloth into a saucepan. Press gently, then discard the grounds.
Reduce: Set the saucepan over low heat and simmer gently until the coffee reduces by half, to about 2 cups. Avoid a hard boil, which can make the flavor bitter.

Dehydrate: Heat the oven to its lowest setting, ideally about 150°F (65°C). Line a rimmed baking sheet with parchment paper and carefully pour the concentrate into an even layer. Dry for several hours, checking regularly, until completely dry and brittle.
Cool and Crush: Let the dried coffee sheet cool completely. Scrape it from the parchment and crush or grind it into fine granules.
Brew: Stir about 1 teaspoon of the powder into 8 ounces of hot water. Add more powder to taste.
Notes
This homemade version is instant-style rather than identical to commercial instant coffee, so a small amount of sediment may remain.
The powder must be completely dry and brittle before storage. If it is soft or tacky, continue drying before sealing it in an airtight container.
A medium roast usually gives the best balance; dark roasts may become bitter during reduction and drying.

title: Sugar-Free Salted Chocolate Caramel Coffee Creamer
lines: Yield: about 2 cups, 16 servings | Serving size: 2 tablespoons
Ingredients
1 cup heavy cream or heavy whipping cream
1 cup unsweetened almond milk
1/3 cup granular monk fruit sweetener or allulose, plus more to taste
2 tablespoons unsweetened cocoa powder, sifted
2 tablespoons sugar-free caramel syrup
1/4 teaspoon kosher salt, plus a tiny pinch if desired
Directions
Combine the heavy cream, almond milk, and sweetener in a small saucepan over medium-low heat.
Sift in the cocoa powder, then add the caramel syrup and salt.
Whisk continuously just until the sweetener and cocoa dissolve and the mixture is smooth. Do not boil.
Remove from the heat. Let a spoonful cool before tasting, then adjust the sweetener or salt if desired.
Cool promptly, transfer to a clean, tightly covered jar or bottle, and refrigerate. Shake well before each use.
Notes
Natural separation is normal; shake before measuring.
Refrigerate at 40°F or colder and use within 4 days, or sooner if any ingredient reaches its use-by date.
Sweeteners and caramel syrups vary in sweetness, so adjust them to taste.

1 cup unsweetened almond milk
1/3 cup granular monk fruit sweetener or allulose, plus more to taste
1 to 2 tablespoons pure vanilla extract, or vanilla bean paste with no added sugar
Directions
Combine the heavy cream, almond milk, and sweetener in a small saucepan over medium-low heat.
Whisk continuously until the sweetener dissolves and the mixture is smooth. Do not boil.
Remove from the heat and stir in 1 tablespoon vanilla. Add the second tablespoon after tasting if a stronger vanilla flavor is desired.
Cool promptly, transfer to a clean, tightly covered jar or bottle, and refrigerate. Shake well before each use.
Notes
Natural separation is normal; shake before measuring.
Refrigerate at 40°F or colder and use within 4 days, or sooner if any ingredient reaches its use-by date.
Whole milk, half-and-half, or oat milk may be substituted for the almond milk; the flavor and texture will vary.

title: Rich Salted Chocolate Caramel Coffee Creamer
lines: Yield: about 2 cups, 16 servings | Serving size: 2 tablespoons
Ingredients
1 cup heavy cream or heavy whipping cream
1 cup whole milk
1/3 cup granular monk fruit sweetener, plus more to taste
2 tablespoons unsweetened cocoa powder, sifted
2 tablespoons regular caramel sauce or syrup
1/4 teaspoon kosher salt, plus a tiny pinch if desired
Directions
Combine the heavy cream, whole milk, and monk fruit sweetener in a small saucepan over medium-low heat.
Sift in the cocoa powder, then add the caramel sauce or syrup and salt.
Whisk continuously just until the sweetener and cocoa dissolve and the mixture is smooth. Do not boil.
Remove from the heat. Let a spoonful cool before tasting, then adjust the sweetener or salt if desired.
Cool promptly, transfer to a clean, tightly covered jar or bottle, and refrigerate. Shake well before each use.
Notes
Natural separation is normal; shake before measuring.
Refrigerate at 40°F or colder and use within 4 days, or sooner if any ingredient reaches its use-by date.
Regular caramel sauces and syrups contain sugar and vary by brand; adjust the monk fruit sweetener after tasting.

title: Failproof Homemade Mayonnaise
lines: Yield: about 1 cup, 16 servings | Serving size: 1 tablespoon
Ingredients
1 large egg
1 tablespoon white wine vinegar or red wine vinegar
1 tablespoon Dijon mustard
1/4 teaspoon fine sea salt, plus more to taste
1 cup (240 milliliters) safflower oil or vegetable oil
1 teaspoon fresh lemon juice, optional
Directions
Add the egg, vinegar, mustard, salt, and optional lemon juice to a tall, narrow jar. Pour the oil on top.
Place the head of an immersion blender firmly against the bottom of the jar, directly over the egg.
Blend on high without lifting the blender. Within about 10 seconds, a thick, white layer should begin forming at the bottom.
Once the mayonnaise forms, slowly lift and lower the blender to incorporate the remaining oil. Blend until thick and creamy, about 20 to 30 seconds total.
Taste and adjust with additional salt, lemon juice, or vinegar.
Notes
Makes about 1 cup. Store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2 weeks. Use a fresh pasteurized egg if raw-egg safety is a concern.
Optional Flavor Variations

Green Tabasco Mayo: After the mayonnaise has fully emulsified, stir in 2 teaspoons Green Tabasco. Use 1 teaspoon for mild flavor or up to 1 tablespoon for a bold, tangy kick. Let it rest for 10 minutes, then taste before adding more salt.

Garlic Aioli Style: After the mayonnaise has fully emulsified, stir in 1 small garlic clove, finely grated or mashed into a smooth paste. Use 2 cloves for a stronger garlic flavor. Let it rest for 15 minutes before tasting because the garlic will grow stronger as it sits. For a Green Tabasco garlic aioli, add 2 teaspoons Green Tabasco along with the garlic.
Source

title: Smooth Homemade Tahini
lines: Yield: about 3/4 cup, 12 servings | Serving size: 1 tablespoon | Active time: about 10 minutes
Ingredients
1 cup hulled white sesame seeds
2 to 4 tablespoons neutral oil, such as avocado oil, grapeseed oil, or light olive oil
Pinch of fine sea salt, optional
Directions

Toast the Seeds: Place the sesame seeds in a dry skillet or saucepan over medium-low heat. Cook for 3 to 5 minutes, stirring constantly, until fragrant and very lightly golden. Do not brown them, or the tahini may taste bitter.
Cool Completely: Immediately transfer the seeds to a plate or baking sheet. Let them cool completely for at least 15 minutes.
Make the Initial Paste: Add the cooled seeds to a food processor or high-speed blender. Process for 1 to 2 minutes, scraping down the sides as needed, until the seeds form a crumbly paste.
Add the Oil: Add 2 tablespoons of the oil and the optional salt. Process for another 2 to 3 minutes, stopping to scrape down the bowl.
Adjust the Texture: With the machine running, drizzle in additional oil a little at a time, using up to 2 more tablespoons, until the tahini is smooth, pourable, and creamy.
Store: Transfer to a clean, airtight glass jar. Refrigerate for up to 1 month and stir well before using if natural separation occurs.
Notes
Hulled sesame seeds create a milder, smoother tahini with less bitterness than unhulled seeds.
Oil needs vary with the sesame seeds and the size and power of the food processor or blender.
Allow about 25 minutes total, including the cooling period.

1: Practical batch recipe — unchanged | Yield: about 3/4 cup, 12 servings | Serving size: 1 tablespoon
This recipe remains at its normal batch size on every serving tab.
Ingredients
1 cup hulled white sesame seeds
2 to 4 tablespoons neutral oil, such as avocado oil, grapeseed oil, or light olive oil
Pinch of fine sea salt, optional
Directions

Toast the Seeds: Place the sesame seeds in a dry skillet or saucepan over medium-low heat. Cook for 3 to 5 minutes, stirring constantly, until fragrant and very lightly golden. Do not brown them, or the tahini may taste bitter.
Cool Completely: Immediately transfer the seeds to a plate or baking sheet. Let them cool completely for at least 15 minutes.
Make the Initial Paste: Add the cooled seeds to a food processor or high-speed blender. Process for 1 to 2 minutes, scraping down the sides as needed, until the seeds form a crumbly paste.
Add the Oil: Add 2 tablespoons of the oil and the optional salt. Process for another 2 to 3 minutes, stopping to scrape down the bowl.
Adjust the Texture: With the machine running, drizzle in additional oil a little at a time, using up to 2 more tablespoons, until the tahini is smooth, pourable, and creamy.
Store: Transfer to a clean, airtight glass jar. Refrigerate for up to 1 month and stir well before using if natural separation occurs.
Notes
Hulled sesame seeds create a milder, smoother tahini with less bitterness than unhulled seeds.
Oil needs vary with the sesame seeds and the size and power of the food processor or blender.
Allow about 25 minutes total, including the cooling period.

title: Five Minute Blender Hollandaise Sauce
lines: Yield: about 1/2 cup, 8 servings | Serving size: 1 tablespoon
Ingredients
3 large egg yolks
1 tablespoon fresh lemon juice, plus more to taste
1 teaspoon Dijon mustard
1/4 teaspoon fine salt
1 pinch cayenne pepper
1/2 cup unsalted butter or ghee, melted and very hot
Directions
Melt the Butter: Microwave the butter in a covered microwave safe container for about 1 minute, or heat it in a small saucepan, until melted and very hot.
Blend the Base: Add the egg yolks, lemon juice, Dijon mustard, salt, and cayenne to a high powered blender. Blend for 5 seconds.
Emulsify: With the blender running on medium high, pour in the hot butter in a very slow, steady stream. Continue blending until the sauce is thick, smooth, and creamy.
Taste and Serve: Taste and add more lemon juice if desired. Pour the sauce into a warm serving bowl and serve immediately.
Notes
Makes about 4 servings.
The butter must be hot, not merely warm, or the sauce may not emulsify.
If the sauce breaks, run the blender and slowly add 1 tablespoon boiling water. Add a second tablespoon only if needed.
If it still will not come together, blend 1 extra egg yolk with 1 teaspoon hot water, then blend it into the broken sauce.
For an immersion blender, combine everything except the butter in a tall, narrow jar. Keep the blender head against the bottom while slowly drizzling in the hot butter.
Hollandaise is best served fresh. If needed, warm it in 15 second microwave intervals or over very low heat, adding a teaspoon of warm water if the sauce begins to tighten.
Source
Adapted from Lisa Bryan.

title: Savory Sausage Gravy for One
lines: Yield: 1 serving | Serving size: about 3/4 cup gravy
Ingredients
3 ounces pork breakfast sausage, about 1 thick patty
1 1/2 tablespoons all-purpose flour
3/4 cup whole milk
1/4 teaspoon garlic powder
1/4 teaspoon onion powder
1/2 teaspoon freshly cracked black pepper, or to taste
2 to 3 drops Worcestershire sauce
Tiny pinch red pepper flakes, optional
Salt, to taste
1 teaspoon butter, optional, if the sausage is very lean
Directions
Cook the sausage in a skillet over medium heat, breaking it into small crumbles, until browned and fully cooked. Leave the rendered fat in the skillet.
Sprinkle the flour over the sausage. Stir constantly for 1 to 2 minutes, until the flour coats the meat and loses its raw smell. If the mixture looks dry, stir in the optional butter.
Slowly pour in the whole milk while stirring constantly to keep the gravy smooth.

Stir in the garlic powder, onion powder, black pepper, Worcestershire sauce, and optional red pepper flakes. Reduce the heat to medium-low and simmer for 4 to 5 minutes, stirring frequently, until thick.
Taste before adding salt. If the gravy is thicker than you like, stir in a small splash of milk. Serve hot over biscuits.
Notes
The gravy continues to thicken as it stands; loosen it with a little milk if needed.
Breakfast sausage and Worcestershire sauce are already salty, so add salt only after tasting.

title: Quick Refrigerator-Pickled Vegetables
lines: Yield: about 1 quart, 8 servings | Serving size: 1/2 cup vegetables
Ingredients
2 to 3 cups mixed vegetables, cut into bite-size pieces or thin slices
2 to 4 garlic cloves, smashed
2 to 4 fresh dill sprigs
1 teaspoon mustard seeds
1 teaspoon black peppercorns
Pinch of red pepper flakes
1 cup white or apple cider vinegar (5% acidity)
1 cup water
1 tablespoon pickling or kosher salt, or up to 2 tablespoons for a saltier brine
1 tablespoon sugar, optional
Directions
Wash the vegetables, trim as needed, and cut into bite-size pieces or thin slices.
Place the garlic, dill, mustard seeds, peppercorns, and red pepper flakes in a clean 1-quart glass jar.
Pack the vegetables snugly into the jar, leaving about 1/2 inch of space at the top.
Combine the vinegar, water, salt, and optional sugar in a small saucepan. Warm over medium heat, stirring just until dissolved, then remove from the heat.
Pour the warm or room-temperature brine over the vegetables until completely covered. Let a warm jar cool briefly, then cover and refrigerate promptly.
Refrigerate for at least 24 to 48 hours before eating.
Notes
Use only vinegar labeled 5% acidity. These are refrigerator pickles, not shelf-stable canned vegetables.
Keep the vegetables submerged and refrigerated at 40 degrees F or colder. Use within 2 months; discard for mold, sliminess, or an off odor.
Source: Oregon State University Extension.

4: Practical batch recipe — unchanged | Yield: about 1 quart, 8 servings | Serving size: 1/2 cup vegetables
Ingredients
2 to 3 cups mixed vegetables, cut into bite-size pieces or thin slices
2 to 4 garlic cloves, smashed
2 to 4 fresh dill sprigs
1 teaspoon mustard seeds
1 teaspoon black peppercorns
Pinch of red pepper flakes
1 cup white or apple cider vinegar (5% acidity)
1 cup water
1 tablespoon pickling or kosher salt, or up to 2 tablespoons for a saltier brine
1 tablespoon sugar, optional
Directions
Wash the vegetables, trim as needed, and cut into bite-size pieces or thin slices.
Place the garlic, dill, mustard seeds, peppercorns, and red pepper flakes in a clean 1-quart glass jar.
Pack the vegetables snugly into the jar, leaving about 1/2 inch of space at the top.
Combine the vinegar, water, salt, and optional sugar in a small saucepan. Warm over medium heat, stirring just until dissolved, then remove from the heat.
Pour the warm or room-temperature brine over the vegetables until completely covered. Let a warm jar cool briefly, then cover and refrigerate promptly.
Refrigerate for at least 24 to 48 hours before eating.

title: Smoky Cayenne Buttermilk Ranch
lines: Yield: about 1 1/2 cups, 12 servings | Serving size: 2 tablespoons
Ingredients
1 cup mayonnaise
1/4 cup sour cream
1/4 cup buttermilk
1 tablespoon parsley, fresh or dried
1 teaspoon dill
2 teaspoons smoked paprika
1/2 teaspoon onion powder
1/2 teaspoon garlic powder
1/2 teaspoon black pepper
1 teaspoon cayenne pepper
Pinch of salt
Directions
Add all the ingredients to a medium bowl or a jar with a tight-fitting lid.
Whisk until completely smooth and blended. If using a jar, seal it tightly and shake well.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes to let the flavors develop. Stir or shake before serving.
Notes
Makes about 1 1/2 cups.
Store in a covered container in the refrigerator for up to 1 week.

title: Pantry-Style Italian Dressing (Large Batch)
lines: Yield: about 2 cups, 32 servings | Serving size: 1 tablespoon
Ingredients
1 cup + 6 tablespoons regular olive oil
7 tablespoons + 1 teaspoon red wine vinegar
2 tablespoons Dijon mustard
1 tablespoon honey
1 tablespoon garlic powder
1 tablespoon onion powder
1 tablespoon dried oregano
1 tablespoon dried basil
1 ½ teaspoons salt (adjust to taste)
1 teaspoon black pepper
½ teaspoon red pepper flakes (optional, for background warmth)
Directions

Whisk the Base: In a large measuring cup or mixing bowl, combine the red wine vinegar, Dijon mustard, honey, and all of your dry seasonings. Whisk thoroughly until the mustard and spices form a smooth paste.
Pour into the Bottle: Insert a funnel into the mouth of your 15.8-ounce squirt bottle. Pour the spiced vinegar mixture straight into the bottom.
Add the Oil: Pour the regular olive oil into the bottle through the funnel.

Shake and Rest: Secure the squirt bottle cap tightly and shake vigorously for 30 to 45 seconds until completely unified. Let it sit at room temperature for 15 minutes before using so the dried herbs can soften and release their flavors.

title: Cold Jalapeño Artichoke Dip
lines: Yield: about 2 1/2 cups, 20 servings | Serving size: 2 tablespoons
Ingredients
1 brick (8 ounces) cream cheese, completely softened
1/2 cup sour cream
1 jar or can marinated artichoke hearts, drained very well, squeezed dry, and finely chopped
2 giant jalapeños, seeded and very finely minced
2 green onions, finely sliced, using both the white and green parts
1 to 2 teaspoons fresh lime juice, starting with 1 teaspoon
2 garlic cloves, minced into a paste
2 to 3 tablespoons fresh dill, finely chopped, or 2 to 3 teaspoons dried dill weed
1/2 teaspoon onion powder
1/4 teaspoon black pepper
Optional: salt, only after tasting, added 1/8 teaspoon at a time
Directions
Dry the Artichokes: Place the chopped marinated artichoke hearts on paper towels and press down firmly to remove excess oil and vinegar.
Blend the Dairy Base: Whip the softened cream cheese and sour cream together in a mixing bowl until perfectly smooth.
Mix in the Flavorings: Fold in the chopped artichoke hearts, jalapeños, green onions, garlic paste, and either the fresh dill or dried dill weed.
Brighten with Lime and Spice: Stir in the onion powder, black pepper, and the first 1 teaspoon of lime juice.
Taste Test: Taste the dip with a chip or cracker. For more brightness, add the second teaspoon of lime juice. If it needs salt, add a tiny pinch, no more than 1/8 teaspoon at a time.

Chill: Seal the dip tightly in an airtight container and refrigerate for at least 1 to 2 hours before eating. This rest is especially helpful when using dried dill weed because it gives the herb time to soften and release its flavor.
Notes
The sour cream is reduced to 1/2 cup because lime juice thins the dairy base.
The lime juice and marinated artichoke hearts add plenty of tang and salt, so do not add salt during mixing. Taste first, then add only a tiny pinch if needed.

title: Savory Guajillo Garlic Cream Sauce
lines: Yield: about 2 cups, 4 servings | Serving size: about 1/2 cup
Ingredients
3 medium dried guajillo chiles, stemmed, seeded, and torn into flat pieces
1 tablespoon unsalted butter
1 tablespoon olive oil
1/2 cup finely diced yellow onion
1 celery stalk, finely diced (about 1/3 cup)
6 garlic cloves, minced
1 small Roma tomato, chopped
1 cup low-sodium chicken broth, plus more as needed
1/2 teaspoon ground cumin
1 teaspoon dried Mexican oregano, crushed
1/2 teaspoon ground black pepper
1/2 teaspoon fine sea salt, plus more to taste
3/4 cup heavy whipping cream
1 teaspoon fresh lime juice
Optional: 1/2 cup finely shredded Monterey Jack or mozzarella
Directions

Prepare the Chiles: Heat a dry skillet over medium. Press each guajillo flat for 5 to 10 seconds per side, just until fragrant and slightly pliable; do not let it smoke or blacken. Cover with very hot water and soak for 20 minutes. Drain and discard the soaking water.

Build the Aromatic Base: Melt the butter with the olive oil in a saucepan over medium heat. Add the onion and celery and cook for 6 to 8 minutes, stirring often, until very soft but not browned. Add the garlic and cook for 30 seconds.

Blend Until Smooth: Add the softened chiles, sautéed vegetables, tomato, broth, cumin, oregano, black pepper, and salt to a blender. Let the mixture cool briefly, vent the lid, and blend for about 1 minute until completely smooth.

Cook the Purée: For an extra-silky sauce, press the mixture through a medium-mesh strainer. Return it to the saucepan and simmer uncovered over medium-low heat for 8 to 10 minutes, stirring occasionally.

Finish with Cream: Reduce the heat to low and slowly stir in the heavy cream. Simmer gently for 3 to 5 minutes without boiling. For a cheesy finish, add the optional cheese a small handful at a time and stir until smooth.

Brighten and Serve: Remove from the heat and stir in the lime juice. Taste and adjust the salt. Thin with a splash of broth if needed, then serve with pasta, chicken, enchiladas, or roasted vegetables.
Notes
Guajillo provides a bright, earthy chile flavor with gentle heat; the lime supplies the sharp finish that keeps the cream from tasting heavy.
For a tomato-free version, omit the Roma tomato and add 1 teaspoon tomato bouillon; reduce the salt at first because bouillon sodium varies by brand.
Very small batches blend best in a narrow blender cup. Refrigerate leftovers promptly and use within 3 days.

title: Deep Pasilla Monterey Jack Cream Sauce
lines: Yield: about 2 cups, 4 servings | Serving size: about 1/2 cup
Ingredients
2 large dried pasilla negro chiles, stemmed, seeded, and torn into flat pieces
1 tablespoon unsalted butter
1 tablespoon olive oil
1/2 cup finely diced yellow onion
1 celery stalk, finely diced (about 1/3 cup)
6 garlic cloves, minced
1 tablespoon tomato paste
1 1/4 cups low-sodium chicken broth, plus more as needed
1/2 teaspoon ground cumin
1 teaspoon dried Mexican oregano, crushed
1/2 teaspoon ground black pepper
1/2 teaspoon fine sea salt, plus more to taste
3/4 cup heavy whipping cream
3/4 cup freshly shredded Monterey Jack
1 teaspoon red wine vinegar
Directions

Prepare the Chiles: Heat a dry skillet over medium. Press each pasilla flat for 5 to 10 seconds per side, just until fragrant and pliable; do not let it smoke or scorch. Cover with very hot water and soak for 20 minutes. Drain and discard the soaking water.

Build the Savory Base: Melt the butter with the olive oil in a saucepan over medium heat. Add the onion and celery and cook for 6 to 8 minutes until very soft. Add the garlic and tomato paste and cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.

Blend Until Smooth: Add the softened pasillas, sautéed mixture, broth, cumin, oregano, black pepper, and salt to a blender. Let the mixture cool briefly, vent the lid, and blend for about 1 minute until completely smooth.

Cook the Purée: For the smoothest sauce, press the mixture through a medium-mesh strainer. Return it to the saucepan and simmer uncovered over medium-low heat for 8 to 10 minutes, stirring occasionally.

Make It Creamy and Cheesy: Reduce the heat to low and slowly stir in the heavy cream. Add the Monterey Jack a small handful at a time, stirring until each addition melts. Keep the sauce below a boil so it stays smooth.

Balance and Serve: Remove from the heat and stir in the red wine vinegar. Taste and adjust the salt and pepper. Thin with a splash of broth if needed, then toss with pasta or spoon over steak, chicken, potatoes, or roasted mushrooms.
Notes
Pasilla gives this sauce a dark, earthy, gently fruity depth; the tomato paste is deliberately restrained so the sauce stays savory.
Freshly shredded cheese melts more smoothly than bagged cheese, which may contain anti-caking ingredients.
Very small batches blend best in a narrow blender cup. Refrigerate leftovers promptly and use within 3 days.

title: Spicy Guajillo–Árbol Crema Sauce
lines: Yield: about 2 cups, 4 servings | Serving size: about 1/2 cup
Ingredients
2 medium dried guajillo chiles, stemmed, seeded, and torn into flat pieces
2 dried chiles de árbol, stemmed
1 tablespoon olive oil
1/2 cup finely diced yellow onion
1/4 cup finely diced celery
5 garlic cloves, minced
1 small Roma tomato, chopped
1/2 cup low-sodium chicken broth, plus more as needed
1/2 teaspoon ground cumin
1/2 teaspoon dried Mexican oregano, crushed
1/4 teaspoon ground black pepper
1/2 teaspoon fine sea salt, plus more to taste
1 cup Mexican crema or full-fat sour cream
1 tablespoon fresh lime juice
Directions

Prepare the Chiles: Heat a dry skillet over medium. Press each guajillo flat for 5 to 10 seconds per side until fragrant. Add the chiles de árbol and stir for only a few seconds. Do not let any chile smoke or blacken. Cover with very hot water and soak for 20 minutes, then drain and discard the soaking water.
Sauté the Aromatics: Heat the olive oil in a saucepan over medium heat. Add the onion and celery and cook for 6 to 8 minutes until very soft but not browned. Add the garlic and cook for 30 seconds.

Blend the Chile Base: Add the softened chiles, sautéed vegetables, tomato, broth, cumin, oregano, black pepper, and salt to a blender. Let the mixture cool briefly, vent the lid, and blend for about 1 minute until completely smooth.

Cook the Purée: For a silky crema, press the mixture through a medium-mesh strainer. Return it to the saucepan and simmer uncovered over medium-low heat for 8 to 10 minutes. Remove from the heat and let it cool for 5 minutes.

Temper the Crema: Whisk a few spoonfuls of the warm chile purée into the crema, then slowly whisk the tempered crema back into the pan. Stir in the lime juice. Warm gently over low heat if needed, but do not boil.
Adjust and Serve: Taste and adjust the salt. Thin with a splash of broth for drizzling, or leave it thick for dipping. Serve with tacos, eggs, grilled chicken, steak, roasted potatoes, or pasta.
Notes
For gentler heat, use 1 chile de árbol; use 2 for a lively medium-hot sauce or 3 for a sharper kick. Chile heat varies from pod to pod.
Wear gloves if your skin is sensitive, and avoid touching your eyes after handling chiles de árbol.
Very small batches blend best in a narrow blender cup. Refrigerate leftovers promptly and use within 3 days.

title: Baked Feta Pasta
lines: Yield: 4 servings | Serving size: 1/4 of the finished recipe
Prep: 10 minutes | Cook: 45 minutes | Total: 55 minutes
Ingredients
2 pints cherry tomatoes (about 4 cups)
1/2 cup extra-virgin olive oil
1 block (8 ounces) feta cheese
1 teaspoon dried oregano
1 teaspoon salt
1/2 teaspoon freshly cracked black pepper
2 teaspoons minced garlic
8 ounces dry pasta
8 fresh basil leaves, torn
1/4 cup chopped fresh parsley
1 teaspoon red pepper flakes, or to taste (optional)
Directions
Heat the oven to 400°F. Place the cherry tomatoes in a 9 x 13-inch baking dish and set the feta in the center.
Sprinkle the oregano, salt, and black pepper over the feta. Pour the olive oil over the cheese and tomatoes, then gently toss the tomatoes to coat.
Bake uncovered for 40 minutes, until the tomatoes are softened and bursting and the feta is soft.
Meanwhile, cook the pasta according to the package directions until al dente. Reserve some pasta cooking water before draining.
Mash the baked feta and tomatoes together. Stir in the minced garlic until combined.
If the sauce is too thick, stir in reserved pasta water a couple of tablespoons at a time. Add the basil, parsley, and cooked pasta and toss well.
Sprinkle with red pepper flakes, if using, and serve hot.
Notes
Use block Greek feta, fresh herbs, and an olive oil you enjoy for the best flavor. Reserve pasta cooking water to loosen the sauce as needed.
Adapted from Baked Feta Pasta by Bella Bucchiotti, xoxoBella. Source: https://xoxobella.com/wprm_print/baked-feta-pasta

title: Texas-Style Chili Cheese Enchiladas
lines: Yield: 12 enchiladas, 6 servings | Serving size: 2 enchiladas
Prep: about 20 minutes | Bake: 30–35 minutes | Rest: 5 minutes
Ingredients
12 small (about 6-inch) corn tortillas
1 pound ground beef
2 cups prepared Tex-Mex chili gravy
2 cups shredded cheddar cheese, divided
1/2 cup diced onion
1 teaspoon chili powder
1/2 teaspoon ground cumin
Salt and black pepper, to taste
A little neutral oil, for greasing and softening tortillas if needed
Directions
Heat the oven to 375°F. Lightly grease a baking dish large enough to hold 12 small enchiladas in one layer.

Cook the ground beef and diced onion in a skillet over medium heat for 7–10 minutes, breaking the meat into small pieces, until the onion is tender and the beef reaches 160°F. Drain excess fat. Stir in the chili powder and cumin, salt, and pepper; cook for 30 seconds.

Warm the corn tortillas in a damp kitchen towel in the microwave in short bursts until soft and pliable; keep covered while filling. If they still split, briefly heat each tortilla on both sides in a lightly oiled skillet.
Warm the chili gravy. Spread a thin layer over the bottom of the baking dish. Stir a spoonful into the beef filling to keep it moist.
Divide the beef mixture and half of the cheddar evenly among the 12 tortillas. Roll tightly and place seam-side down in the baking dish.
Spoon the remaining chili gravy evenly over the rolls, covering the edges. Sprinkle with the remaining cheddar.
Cover loosely with foil and bake for 20 minutes. Uncover and bake for another 10–15 minutes, until bubbly, the cheese is melted, and the center reaches 165°F.
Rest for 5 minutes before serving. Serve 2 enchiladas per person.
Notes
Use a snug baking dish: about 9 x 13 inches for the full batch, or two smaller dishes if needed. For 1–2 servings, use a small casserole dish; keep the enchiladas in one layer.
Baking time depends on the dish and filling temperature. Start checking smaller batches about 5 minutes early and bake until the center reaches 165°F.

Quick homemade chili gravy for this batch (instead of the prepared gravy): Heat 3 tablespoons neutral oil in a saucepan. Whisk in 3 tablespoons all-purpose flour and cook for 1–2 minutes. Stir in 2 tablespoons mild chili powder, 1/2 teaspoon ground cumin, and 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder for 20 seconds. Gradually whisk in 2 cups beef broth. Simmer 5–8 minutes, stirring, until lightly thickened. Season to taste with salt; thin with water if needed. This makes about 2 cups gravy.
Source
Ingredient lists adapted from the Quick Fix Recipes graphic supplied by Corey. Cooking directions and serving-size scaling developed for this cookbook; these are not verified publisher instructions.

title: Chicken Bacon Ranch Enchiladas
lines: Yield: 12 enchiladas, 6 servings | Serving size: 2 enchiladas
Prep: about 20 minutes | Bake: 25–30 minutes | Rest: 5 minutes
Ingredients
3 cups cooked shredded chicken
6 slices bacon, cooked and crumbled, divided
12 small (about 6-inch) flour tortillas
1 cup ranch dressing
2 cups shredded Monterey Jack cheese, divided
1/2 cup sour cream
2 green onions, sliced, divided
1/2 teaspoon garlic powder
Black pepper, to taste
A little neutral oil or cooking spray, for greasing
Directions
Heat the oven to 350°F. Lightly grease a baking dish large enough to hold 12 small enchiladas in one layer.
Whisk the ranch dressing, sour cream, garlic powder, and black pepper together. If too thick to spread, stir in water a teaspoon at a time.
Combine the chicken with one-third of the ranch mixture, half of the Monterey Jack, most of the bacon, and half of the sliced green onions. Reserve the remaining bacon and green onions for topping.
Warm the flour tortillas in a damp kitchen towel in the microwave in short bursts until soft and pliable; keep covered while filling.
Spread a thin coating of the remaining ranch mixture in the baking dish. Divide the chicken filling evenly among the 12 tortillas, roll them, and arrange seam-side down.
Spread the remaining ranch mixture over the rolls and sprinkle with the remaining cheese. Cover with foil and bake for 20 minutes.
Uncover and bake for 5–10 minutes more, until the cheese is melted and the filling reaches 165°F. Add time if the chicken started refrigerator-cold.
Rest for 5 minutes, then scatter the reserved bacon and green onions on top. Serve 2 enchiladas per person.
Notes
Use a snug baking dish: about 9 x 13 inches for the full batch, or two smaller dishes if needed. For 1–2 servings, use a small casserole dish; keep the enchiladas in one layer.
Baking time depends on the dish and filling temperature. Start checking smaller batches about 5 minutes early and bake until the center reaches 165°F.
Use fully cooked chicken and bacon. A thick bottled ranch dressing works well; taste before adding salt because the dressing, bacon, and cheese are already salty.

title: Creamy White Chicken Enchiladas
lines: Yield: 12 enchiladas, 6 servings | Serving size: 2 enchiladas
Prep: about 20 minutes | Bake: 25–30 minutes | Rest: 5 minutes
Ingredients
3 cups cooked shredded chicken
12 small (about 6-inch) flour tortillas
3 tablespoons butter
3 tablespoons all-purpose flour
2 cups chicken broth
1 cup sour cream
2 cups shredded Monterey Jack cheese, divided
1/2 teaspoon garlic powder
Salt and black pepper, to taste
A little neutral oil or cooking spray, for greasing
Directions
Heat the oven to 375°F. Lightly grease a baking dish large enough to hold 12 small enchiladas in one layer.
Melt the butter in a saucepan over medium heat. Whisk in the flour and cook, stirring, for 1–2 minutes without browning.

Gradually whisk in the chicken broth until smooth. Bring to a gentle simmer and cook for 3–5 minutes, stirring often, until the sauce lightly coats a spoon. Remove from the heat and let cool for 2 minutes.

Whisk a few spoonfuls of warm sauce into the sour cream, then gradually whisk this mixture back into the saucepan. Stir in the garlic powder, salt, and pepper. Do not boil the sauce after adding sour cream.
Warm the flour tortillas in a damp kitchen towel in the microwave in short bursts until soft and pliable; keep covered while filling.
Mix the chicken with half of the Monterey Jack and a small spoonful of sauce. Spread a thin layer of sauce over the bottom of the baking dish.
Divide the filling among the 12 tortillas, roll, and place seam-side down. Pour the remaining sauce over the rolls and top with the remaining cheese.
Cover with foil and bake for 20 minutes. Uncover and bake for another 5–10 minutes, until the sauce bubbles gently, the cheese melts, and the filling reaches 165°F.
Rest for 5 minutes before serving. Serve 2 enchiladas per person.

Use a snug baking dish: about 9 x 13 inches for the full batch, or two smaller dishes if needed. For 1–2 servings, use a small casserole dish; keep the enchiladas in one layer.

title: Pie Tin Enchiladas
lines: Estimated yield: 6 small pies, 12 servings | Serving size: 1/2 pie
Prep: about 25 minutes | Bake: about 20-30 minutes | Rest: 5 minutes
Equipment
Small oven-safe pie tins or pie plates, about 6-7 inches across; use 3 tortillas per pie.
A sturdy rimmed baking sheet to support the pie tins.
Ingredients
2 (10-ounce) cans red enchilada sauce; mild is Corey's choice
1 pound ground beef or turkey
1 taco seasoning packet (assumed 1 ounce), plus package-directed water
32 ounces shredded fiesta blend cheese, or a mix of Pepper Jack and medium cheddar
1 can Rosarita refried beans (assumed 16 ounces)
18 small (about 6-inch) white or yellow corn tortillas, from 1 package
1 medium red or yellow onion, diced
1 can sliced black olives (assumed 2.25 ounces), drained
Directions
Place an oven rack in the center and heat the oven to 350 F. Set 6 small oven-safe pie tins on sturdy rimmed baking sheets.
Dice the onion, drain the olives, and shred the cheese if needed. Divide the beans, meat, onion, cheese, and sauce evenly among the pies as you assemble them.

Brown the ground beef or turkey in a skillet, breaking it into crumbles. Check with a food thermometer: ground beef must reach 160 F and ground turkey 165 F. Drain excess grease. Stir in the taco seasoning and the package-directed water in proportion to the amount used; simmer until the meat is seasoned and no longer watery.
Warm the enchilada sauce in a small saucepan over low heat without boiling. Warm the refried beans separately over low heat, stirring often.
Briefly dip a corn tortilla into the warm sauce with tongs and lay it in a pie tin. Spread on the beans, then add about half of that pie's meat, some onion, and a little cheese.

Dip a second tortilla into the sauce and place it over the filling. Add the remaining meat for that pie, more onion, and a little cheese. Dip a third tortilla and place it on top. Spoon over any remaining sauce, then top with the remaining cheese and sliced olives.

Repeat for the remaining pies. Keep the tins on the baking sheet for support. Bake for an estimated 20-30 minutes, until the cheese has melted, the edges bubble, and the center reaches 165 F. Time varies with tin size and filling temperature; use the thermometer as the final check.
Rest for 5 minutes. Cut each pie in half; one half-pie is one serving. Voila! Pie Tin Enchiladas.
Notes

Working yield: 6 small pies, cut into 12 half-pie servings. The original PDF does not specify tin size, tortilla count, can sizes, baking time, or yield; these are cookbook planning estimates and have not been kitchen-tested.
The original 32 ounces of cheese is retained. This makes a very rich dish; one whole pie counts as two of the servings listed here.

Estimated total carbohydrate: about 25-35 g per half-pie serving, or 50-70 g per whole pie. This estimate assumes standard 6-inch corn tortillas, a 16-ounce can of refried beans, and a 2.25-ounce can of olives in the full batch. Tortillas, beans, sauce, seasoning, and cheese brands change the count; calculate from your labels for greater accuracy.
Use white or yellow corn tortillas and mild red enchilada sauce, or choose a hotter sauce if you prefer. Pepper Jack and medium cheddar can replace the fiesta blend.
For 1, 3, or 5 people, the scaled recipe makes one extra half-pie portion so no tortilla needs to be halved before assembly.
Source

Corey Kite's uploaded Pie Tin Enchiladas Recipe.pdf. Original ingredients and three-tortilla layering preserved; assumed package sizes, portion guide, baking-time estimate, and serving-size batches added for this cookbook.
Safe cooking temperatures: https://www.foodsafety.gov/food-safety-charts/safe-minimum-internal-temperatures

5 1/3 ounces (151 g) ground beef or turkey
1/3 of a 1-ounce taco seasoning packet (about 9 g), plus its proportional package-directed water
10 2/3 ounces (302 g) shredded fiesta blend cheese, or a mix of Pepper Jack and medium cheddar
5 1/3 ounces (151 g) refried beans
6 small (about 6-inch) white or yellow corn tortillas
1/3 medium red or yellow onion, diced
About 3/4 ounce (21 g) canned sliced black olives, drained
Directions
Place an oven rack in the center and heat the oven to 350 F. Set 2 small oven-safe pie tins on sturdy rimmed baking sheets.
Dice the onion, drain the olives, and shred the cheese if needed. Divide the beans, meat, onion, cheese, and sauce evenly among the pies as you assemble them.

Brown the ground beef or turkey in a skillet, breaking it into crumbles. Check with a food thermometer: ground beef must reach 160 F and ground turkey 165 F. Drain excess grease. Stir in the taco seasoning and the package-directed water in proportion to the amount used; simmer until the meat is seasoned and no longer watery.
Warm the enchilada sauce in a small saucepan over low heat without boiling. Warm the refried beans separately over low heat, stirring often.
Briefly dip a corn tortilla into the warm sauce with tongs and lay it in a pie tin. Spread on the beans, then add about half of that pie's meat, some onion, and a little cheese.

Dip a second tortilla into the sauce and place it over the filling. Add the remaining meat for that pie, more onion, and a little cheese. Dip a third tortilla and place it on top. Spoon over any remaining sauce, then top with the remaining cheese and sliced olives.

Repeat for the remaining pies. Keep the tins on the baking sheet for support. Bake for an estimated 20-30 minutes, until the cheese has melted, the edges bubble, and the center reaches 165 F. Time varies with tin size and filling temperature; use the thermometer as the final check.
Rest for 5 minutes. Cut each pie in half; one half-pie is one serving. Voila! Pie Tin Enchiladas.

The original 32 ounces of cheese is retained. This makes a very rich dish; one whole pie counts as two of the servings listed here.

Estimated total carbohydrate: about 25-35 g per half-pie serving, or 50-70 g per whole pie. This estimate assumes standard 6-inch corn tortillas, a 16-ounce can of refried beans, and a 2.25-ounce can of olives in the full batch. title: Corey's Pie Tin Ground Beef Crema Enchiladas
lines: Estimated yield: 6 small pies, 12 servings. Serving size: 1/2 pie.
Prep: about 30 minutes | Bake: 25-30 minutes | Rest: 5 minutes
Three corn-tortilla layers with seasoned beef, refried beans, green chile lime crema, melted Monterey Jack, and olives.
Equipment
Six shallow 6-7-inch oven-safe pie tins, a sturdy rimmed baking sheet, a skillet, and a saucepan.
Ingredients
1 teaspoon olive oil
1 pound lean ground beef
1 medium yellow or red onion, finely diced
2 garlic cloves, minced
1 (about 1-ounce) packet taco seasoning, plus its package-directed water
3 tablespoons unsalted butter
3 tablespoons all-purpose flour
2 cups low-sodium chicken broth
1 cup Mexican crema or full-fat sour cream
1 (4-ounce) can mild diced green chilies, with juices
1 tablespoon fresh lime juice
1/4 cup chopped fresh cilantro, optional
Salt and black pepper, to taste
18 small (about 6-inch) corn tortillas
1 (16-ounce) can refried beans, warmed
8 ounces Monterey Jack, freshly shredded (about 2 cups), divided
1 (2.25-ounce) can sliced black olives, drained
Optional finish: cilantro, lime wedges, or a little extra crema
Directions
Heat the oven to 350 F. Lightly grease the pie tins and set them on a sturdy rimmed baking sheet.

Heat the oil in a skillet. Soften the onion for 3-4 minutes. Add the beef and garlic; crumble and cook the beef to 160 F. Drain excess fat. Add taco seasoning and its package-directed water; simmer until the mixture is moist without loose liquid.
Melt the butter in a saucepan. Whisk in the flour; stir for 1 minute. Slowly whisk in the broth and simmer 3-5 minutes, until lightly thickened. Remove from the heat and let stand for 2 minutes.

Stir 1/2 cup of the cheese into the warm sauce. In a bowl, whisk a few spoonfuls of sauce into the crema; stir that mixture back into the saucepan. Add the green chilies, lime juice, and optional cilantro. Season to taste. Keep warm without boiling.
Warm the tortillas in a damp kitchen towel in short microwave bursts until flexible. Divide the beef, beans, sauce, and remaining 1 1/2 cups cheese into six equal shares.

For each tin, spread a little sauce in the bottom. Add tortilla one, all of that pie's beans, half its beef, some sauce, and a little cheese. Add tortilla two, the remaining beef, more sauce, and a little cheese. Finish with tortilla three, the rest of its sauce and cheese, and olives. Repeat for all six tins.
Cover loosely with foil and bake 15 minutes. Uncover and bake 10-15 minutes more, until the centers reach 165 F and the edges bubble gently. Keep the tins on the baking sheet when moving them.
Rest 5 minutes. Cut each pie in half and serve one half per serving. Add optional garnishes.
Notes
This is a new recipe adaptation. Tin depth and tortilla size affect yield and baking time; check both during the first kitchen test.
Use full-fat crema or sour cream and add it off the heat for a smoother sauce. Add a splash of broth if the sauce becomes too thick to spread.
Estimated total carbohydrate: about 25-35 g per half pie, or 50-70 g per whole pie. Tortillas, beans, seasoning, and dairy brands change the estimate; optional garnishes are not included.
For 1, 3, or 5 people, the scaled recipe makes one extra half-pie portion so no tortilla needs to be halved before assembly.
