lines: Yield: 4 main-dish servings | Serving size: 1/4 of the cooked chicken and marinade
Prep: 15 minutes | Marinate: 6-24 hours | Cook: about 50-60 minutes | Rest: 5 minutes
Ingredients
1 kg (about 2.2 pounds) bone-in chicken legs or quarters, skin removed
1 cup thick plain unsweetened yogurt, preferably Greek
2 tablespoons lemon juice
2 tablespoons ginger-garlic paste
1 tablespoon tandoori masala
1 teaspoon red chili powder; Kashmiri is a milder choice
1 teaspoon salt, or less if the masala contains salt
1 tablespoon neutral cooking oil, plus a little for the rack
1 teaspoon garam masala
1 tablespoon butter, melted, optional for finishing
Red food coloring, optional; follow its label
Directions
Pat the chicken dry without rinsing it. Cut 2-3 slits into the thickest flesh of each piece to help the marinade penetrate.

Stir the yogurt, lemon juice, ginger-garlic paste, tandoori masala, chili powder, salt, oil, garam masala, and optional food coloring together. Coat the chicken thoroughly, including the slits. Cover and refrigerate 6-24 hours; overnight gives fuller flavor.

Heat the oven to 350 F (180 C). Line a rimmed baking sheet with foil and set a lightly oiled oven-safe wire rack on top. Arrange the chicken with space between the pieces, leaving excess loose marinade in the bowl. Discard that used marinade.
Bake 20 minutes, turn the chicken, and bake another 20 minutes.

Raise the oven to 450 F (230 C). Roast about 10-15 minutes more, until browned and the thickest flesh reaches at least 165 F (74 C), measured away from bone. Larger quarters may need longer; temperature, rather than color or timing alone, determines doneness.
For extra browned spots, optionally broil 1-3 minutes, watching constantly and keeping the chicken clear of the heating element.
Brush the cooked chicken with the optional melted butter. Rest 5 minutes before dividing into the stated servings.
Notes

The graphic says 4-6 servings. This cookbook uses 4 main-dish servings per 1 kg of raw bone-in chicken for consistent scaling; divide the cooked chicken into equal portions. The bone and cooking loss are not edible serving weight.

Lower-carb guide: estimated 4-7 g total carbohydrate per serving, counting a proportional share of all the marinade. Plain yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, and spice-blend brands vary. Rice, naan, chutneys, and other sides are not included.

Choose unsweetened plain thick yogurt. Kashmiri red chili powder gives color with gentler heat; hot Indian chili powder is much spicier. American chili seasoning is a different spice blend. Red food coloring is optional and can be omitted.
For the full batch, 1 tablespoon finely grated ginger plus 1 tablespoon minced garlic can replace the 2 tablespoons combined paste. Reduce salt if your tandoori masala already contains salt.

Keep pieces similar in size. A smaller batch does not automatically cook faster; check the thickest piece with a thermometer. A home oven gives browned edges but not the full charcoal-smoked flavor of a tandoor.
Source

title: Creamy White Chicken Chili
lines: Yield: 5 servings | Serving size: 1/5 of the finished pot, divided evenly
Prep: 10 minutes | Cook: about 25-30 minutes | Method: stovetop
A comforting white chicken chili with a velvety broth thickened by mashed beans, without canned cream soup.
Ingredients
1 tablespoon olive oil
1 yellow onion, diced
3 garlic cloves, minced
4 cups low-sodium chicken broth
1 (4-ounce) can diced green chilies
1 teaspoon ground cumin
1/4 teaspoon cayenne pepper, or to taste
1 teaspoon dried oregano
1/4 teaspoon paprika
Salt and black pepper, to taste
2 (15-ounce) cans Great Northern or cannellini beans, rinsed and drained, divided
3 cups shredded cooked chicken; rotisserie works well
1/2 cup sour cream or plain Greek yogurt
1 tablespoon fresh lime juice
1 1/2 cups frozen or fresh corn, optional
Directions
Heat the olive oil in a pot over medium heat. Cook the onion for about 5 minutes, until soft. Add the garlic, cumin, cayenne, oregano, paprika, salt, and black pepper; cook for 1 minute.
Pour in the chicken broth and diced green chilies. Add three-quarters of the drained beans. In the full five-serving batch, that is one full can plus half of the second can.

Mash the remaining quarter of the beans thoroughly with a fork, or blend with a little of the broth. Stir the puree into the pot. Bring just to a gentle boil, reduce the heat, and simmer for 15 minutes.
Stir in the cooked shredded chicken and the optional corn. Simmer for another 5-10 minutes, until the chicken is hot throughout.
Remove from the heat. Stir in the sour cream or Greek yogurt and the lime juice. Divide into the stated number of servings and add any optional toppings.
Notes

To keep the sour cream or Greek yogurt smooth, take the pot off the heat before adding it. Stir a little warm broth into the dairy first if it is very cold, then stir it into the pot. Do not boil after adding the dairy.
Optional toppings: shredded Monterey Jack, fresh cilantro, or crushed tortilla chips. Toppings are not included in the carbohydrate estimate.

Estimated total carbohydrate per serving: roughly 30-40 g without the optional corn, or 40-50 g with it. These are estimates for one-fifth of the full batch, without toppings; bean, broth, dairy, and corn brands can change the count.
For smaller batches, spoon measures, garlic, and shredded-chicken amounts are rounded slightly for practical cooking. Add a splash of broth if the chili is thicker than you like.

For a fractional can, weigh its contents and use the fraction listed. Weigh the beans after rinsing and draining; use the green chilies with their juices. Mash one-quarter of the total beans and leave the other three-quarters whole.
Source
Recipe and stovetop method supplied by Corey. Serving-size adaptations, practical measuring notes, and approximate carbohydrate estimates added for the website.

Example corn nutrition label: https://greengiantvegetables.com/products/canned-corn/whole-kernel-sweet-corn/

1/8 teaspoon cayenne pepper, or to taste
5/8 teaspoon dried oregano
1/8 teaspoon paprika
Salt and black pepper, to taste
The beans from one 15-ounce can plus 1/5 of a second can Great Northern or cannellini beans, rinsed and drained, divided
1 3/4 cups shredded cooked chicken; rotisserie works well
1/4 cup plus 2 1/2 teaspoons sour cream or plain Greek yogurt
1 3/4 teaspoons fresh lime juice
3/4 cup plus 2 tablespoons plus 1 teaspoon frozen or fresh corn, optional
Directions
Heat the olive oil in a pot over medium heat. Cook the onion for about 5 minutes, until soft. Add the garlic, cumin, cayenne, oregano, paprika, salt, and black pepper; cook for 1 minute.
Pour in the chicken broth and diced green chilies. Add three-quarters of the drained beans. In the full five-serving batch, that is one full can plus half of the second can.

Mash the remaining quarter of the beans thoroughly with a fork, or blend with a little of the broth. Stir the puree into the pot. Bring just to a gentle boil, reduce the heat, and simmer for 15 minutes.
Stir in the cooked shredded chicken and the optional corn. Simmer for another 5-10 minutes, until the chicken is hot throughout.
Remove from the heat. Stir in the sour cream or Greek yogurt and the lime juice. Divide into the stated number of servings and add any optional toppings.
Notes

To keep the sour cream or Greek yogurt smooth, take the pot off the heat before adding it. Stir a little warm broth into the dairy first if it is very cold, then stir it into the pot. Do not boil after adding the dairy.
Optional toppings: shredded Monterey Jack, fresh cilantro, or crushed tortilla chips. Toppings are not included in the carbohydrate estimate.

Estimated total carbohydrate per serving: roughly 30-40 g without the optional corn, or 40-50 g with it. These are estimates for one-fifth of the full batch, without toppings; bean, broth, dairy, and corn brands can change the count.
For smaller batches, spoon measures, garlic, and shredded-chicken amounts are rounded slightly for practical cooking. Add a splash of broth if the chili is thicker than you like.

For a fractional can, weigh its contents and use the fraction listed. Weigh the beans after rinsing and draining; use the green chilies with their juices. Mash one-quarter of the total beans and leave the other three-quarters whole.
